title: [Auth] AuthInterceptor outside RedirectInterceptor loses the token on an A->B->A redirect chain, unlike the reverse order
body:
## Summary
RedirectInterceptor strips Authorization on a cross-origin hop and later hops derive from the stripped request. With AuthInterceptor outside RedirectInterceptor nothing re-adds the token on a hop back to the bound origin, while the reverse order does. The class remarks, InterceptorOrdering.cs and Interceptors.md state that both orders are equivalent, so users who choose the outer order get an unexpected 401.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/AuthInterceptor.cs:59`

## Problem
With Auth outside Redirect the token is attached once to the first request (AuthInterceptor.cs:65-76); RedirectInterceptor strips Authorization on the cross-origin hop (RedirectInterceptor.cs:133-138) and every later hop is derived from the stripped request (RedirectHandler.cs:207-211, 238), so nothing re-adds it. With Auth inside Redirect, IsBoundOrigin re-attaches on a hop back to the bound origin. The class remarks say "Redirects back to the original origin carry the credential again" (AuthInterceptor.cs:18-19) and InterceptorOrdering.cs:41-42 and Interceptors.md say the two interceptors work in either order. AuthRedirectOrderTests covers A->B and A->B->B in both orders but not A->B->A.

**Failure scenario.** Order { AuthInterceptor, RedirectInterceptor }: https://api.example.com/x -> 302 https://sso.example.net/check -> 302 https://api.example.com/x?ok=1. The last hop has no Authorization and returns 401; the reversed order returns 200.

## Suggested fix
Either document that only the canonical order keeps the credential on a return hop, or make the outer case equivalent (for example by letting the redirect handler notify outer interceptors of hop requests through the observer contract, as it does for cookies). Add the A->B->A case to AuthRedirectOrderTests for both orders.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Either both orders attach the token on a hop back to the original origin, or the documentation and class remarks state that only the canonical order does
- [ ] The documented ordering guarantee matches the implemented behaviour
- [ ] AuthRedirectOrderTests covers A->B->A in both interceptor orders
- [ ] A a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.

title: [Auth] AuthInterceptor attaches the bearer token to plain http:// requests
body:
## Summary
AuthInterceptor adds the token to any request on the bound origin and the origin check accepts any scheme. Cleartext requests are allowed by default in the Editor and on standalone players, so a typo or http BaseUrl sends the bearer token unencrypted or through an http forward proxy. Issue #56 asked for no injection over plain http unless explicitly allowed, but only the origin binding was implemented.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/AuthInterceptor.cs:59`

## Problem
Wrap (57-76) attaches the token whenever the request is on the bound origin; IsBoundOrigin (112-128) compares scheme, host and port with the first request but accepts any scheme. Cleartext requests are allowed by default in the Editor and on standalone players (Core/CleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:29-42). Issue #56's fix list included 'never inject over plain http unless explicitly allowed'; only the origin binding was implemented.

**Failure scenario.** A standalone build calls `client.Get("http://api.example.com/...")` (a typo, a config value, or an http BaseUrl) through a client with AuthInterceptor: the bearer token crosses the network in cleartext, or through an http forward proxy.

## Spec reference
RFC 6750 section 5.3; RFC 7617 section 4

## Suggested fix
Skip (or fail) for non-https, non-loopback request URIs unless an explicit constructor option allows it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AuthInterceptor does not attach the token to non-https, non-loopback request URIs by default (it skips or fails with a defined UHttpError)
- [ ] An explicit constructor option allows cleartext injection
- [ ] A a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Auth] AuthInterceptor has no target scope and overwrites an explicit per-request Authorization header
body:
## Summary
The interceptor binds to the origin of the first request seen per RequestContext, so every new request binds to its own URL and the provider token goes to whatever origin is addressed. It also replaces an existing Authorization header via WithHeader, unlike DefaultHeadersInterceptor and DecompressionInterceptor. A client shared between the game API and a third-party endpoint leaks the OAuth token to the third party.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/AuthInterceptor.cs:118`

## Problem
IsBoundOrigin binds to the origin of the first request seen on each RequestContext (AuthInterceptor.cs:112-123), so the 'origin' the credential is bound to is simply the URL of every new request; AuthRedirectOrderTests.cs:107-131 (SeparateRequests_EachBindToTheirOwnOrigin) asserts that https://a.test and https://b.test both receive the same bearer token. The constructor takes only a provider and a scheme (AuthInterceptor.cs:42). The header is written with WithHeader, which replaces an existing value (AuthInterceptor.cs:73-74, UHttpRequest.cs:175-180), while DefaultHeadersInterceptor and DecompressionInterceptor respect an existing header and CookieInterceptor merges. Documentation~/Modules/Auth.md recommends WithBearerToken for single requests without saying the interceptor wins.

**Failure scenario.** One UHttpClient with AuthInterceptor(OAuthTokenProvider) is used for the game API and for a CDN or analytics endpoint: the OAuth access token is sent to the third party on every direct request. client.Get(otherApi).WithBearerToken(otherToken) sends the provider's token to the other API instead of the one the caller set.

## Spec reference
RFC 6750 section 5.3

## Suggested fix
Let the interceptor be constructed with the origins (or a predicate) it may authenticate, and skip requests that already carry Authorization unless told to override. Keep the per-context binding only as the redirect guard it was added for.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AuthInterceptor can be constructed with the origins (or a predicate) it may authenticate and does not attach the token to other origins
- [ ] A request that already carries Authorization is left unchanged unless an override option is set
- [ ] The per-context binding remains as the redirect guard
- [ ] A a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-design-11` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. IsBoundOrigin stores the first URI seen per RequestContext and returns true (Runtime/Auth/AuthInterceptor.cs:118-123), so every new request binds to its own origin; the constructor has no origin/predicate parameter (AuthInterceptor.cs:42). Tests/Runtime/Auth/AuthRedirectOrderTests.cs:106-131 asserts https://a.test and https://b.test both receive 'Bearer secret-token'. Explicit header is overwritten: WithBearerToken sets Authorization via WithHeader (AuthBuilderExtensions.cs:15), then the interceptor copies the request and calls WithHeader("Authorization", ...) (AuthInterceptor.cs:73-74), which is HttpHeaders.Set = replace (UHttpRequest.cs:175-180, HttpHeaders.cs:36-44). No test covers a pre-set Authorization, and Documentation~/Modules/Auth.md recommends WithBearerToken for single requests right after the interceptor section without saying the interceptor wins. The only opt-out is the internal SkipAuthMetadataKey (AuthInterceptor.cs:32; reachable only by passing the literal string to the public WithMetadata, undocumented). Closed #56 proposed an allowed-origin set (default: first request/base URI) and no injection over plain http; only the per-context redirect guard was implemented, and no open issue tracks the rest. Client-wide token attachment matches common HTTP-library behaviour, so the cross-origin part is a design gap against the repo's own 'credentials stay with their origin' rule, not a regression; the silent replacement of a caller-set Authorization is plain wrong behaviour.

Related: [[R11-mw-protocol-19]].

title: [Auth] OAuthClient sends redirect_uri as Uri.ToString(), which adds a slash and unescapes, so it differs from the registered value
body:
## Summary
OAuthClient builds redirect_uri in the authorization request and the code exchange from RedirectUri.ToString(). Uri.ToString() appends a slash to authority-only URIs and unescapes, so http://localhost:7890 becomes http://localhost:7890/. Providers that compare redirect URIs by exact string (RFC 6749 section 3.1.2.3), such as Keycloak and Okta, reject the request, which affects loopback and custom-scheme redirects.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:67`

## Problem
CreateAuthorizationRequestAsync uses `config.RedirectUri.ToString()` (OAuthClient.cs:67) and ExchangeCodeAsync falls back to the same (133). Uri.ToString() is the canonically unescaped form: checked on .NET 8, `http://localhost:7890` -> `http://localhost:7890/`, `myapp://callback?x=a%20b` -> `myapp://callback/?x=a b`, `...&x=%41` -> `...&x=A`. RFC 6749 section 3.1.2.3 requires the value to match the registered URI by simple string comparison, and RFC 8252 section 7.3 loopback redirects commonly have no path. Token and discovery URLs are also built with ToString() (234, 322). Tests use only `myapp://oauth/callback`, which ToString() leaves unchanged (OAuthClientTests.cs:454).

**Failure scenario.** A desktop build registers `http://localhost:7890` (or `http://127.0.0.1:7890`) at an exact-match provider (Keycloak, Okta). The authorization request carries `redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A7890%2F` and the provider rejects it as an unregistered redirect URI.

## Spec reference
RFC 6749 sections 3.1.2.3, 4.1.3; RFC 8252 section 7.3

## Suggested fix
Send `RedirectUri.OriginalString` (the string the application registered) in both the authorization and the token request, and use AbsoluteUri/OriginalString for endpoint URLs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] redirect_uri in the authorization request and the token exchange equals the string the application registered (OriginalString)
- [ ] Endpoint URLs are built without altering the configured value
- [ ] Cases http://localhost:7890, myapp://callback and a percent-encoded query are preserved byte for byte
- [ ] A a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-protocol-13` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: redirect_uri is config.RedirectUri.ToString() in the authorization request (OAuthClient.cs:67) and as the fallback in the code exchange (:133). Checked on .NET 8: 'http://localhost:7890' -> 'http://localhost:7890/', 'http://127.0.0.1:7890' -> '.../', '?x=%41' -> '?x=A', and also the common custom-scheme form 'myapp://callback' -> 'myapp://callback/' and 'com.example.app://callback' -> '.../' (wider than the finding states); 'myapp://oauth/callback' (the only test value, OAuthClientTests.cs:454) and 'com.example.app:/oauth2redirect' are unchanged. An exact-match provider rejects the altered value (RFC 6749 section 3.1.2.3). The authorization request has no override; ExchangeCodeAsync accepts request.RedirectUri as a string. Token and discovery URLs also go through ToString() (:234, :322). Not run on Unity Mono.

Also reported as `mw-design-18` (merged into this issue).

title: [Auth] OAuthConfig.UseOidcDiscovery has no effect and the documented discovery flow throws on empty endpoints
body:
## Summary
The flag is read only by ResolveEndpointsAsync, where it turns an explicit call into a no-op. The authorization, exchange and refresh methods call Validate(), which throws when either endpoint is null regardless of the flag, and no flow performs discovery. Auth.md tells developers to set the flag to resolve endpoints from the discovery document, so following it throws ArgumentNullException.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:99`

## Problem
The only reader of UseOidcDiscovery is ResolveEndpointsAsync, which returns the config unchanged when it is false (OAuthClient.cs:99-100). CreateAuthorizationRequestAsync, ExchangeCodeAsync and RefreshTokenAsync call config.Validate(), which throws when AuthorizationEndpoint or TokenEndpoint is null regardless of the flag (OAuthConfig.cs:36-39), and never discover. OAuthConfig has no issuer or discovery-endpoint property; the discovery URI is a separate method argument. Documentation~/Modules/Auth.md says "Set OAuthConfig.UseOidcDiscovery to resolve the endpoints from the issuer's discovery document".

**Failure scenario.** A developer sets UseOidcDiscovery = true and leaves the endpoints empty as the documentation suggests: CreateAuthorizationRequestAsync throws ArgumentNullException(AuthorizationEndpoint). With placeholder endpoints filled in, the placeholders are used and no discovery happens.

## Suggested fix
Remove the flag (calling ResolveEndpointsAsync is the opt-in) or make it real: add the issuer to OAuthConfig, let Validate accept missing endpoints when discovery is requested, and resolve lazily. Correct the documentation sentence.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] UseOidcDiscovery is removed, or implemented so that Validate accepts missing endpoints when discovery is requested and endpoints are resolved lazily
- [ ] Documentation~/Modules/Auth.md describes the actual behaviour
- [ ] A a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

title: [Auth] OAuthClient keeps one SemaphoreSlim per token-store key forever
body:
## Summary
RefreshTokenAsync adds a SemaphoreSlim to a dictionary per key and nothing removes entries, not the invalid_grant path and not Dispose. With keys chosen per user or per scope set, a long-running process grows the dictionary without bound.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:164`

## Problem
`_refreshGuards.GetOrAdd(key, _ => new SemaphoreSlim(1, 1))` (OAuthClient.cs:164) is the only writer of the dictionary declared at 24-25; nothing removes an entry, not the invalid_grant path that removes the token (193), not Dispose (302-313, which leaves the dictionary intact on purpose). Keys are caller-chosen (TokenStoreKey, or clientId|endpoint|scope from BuildTokenStoreKey, 276-281).

**Failure scenario.** A long-running app or server-side tool that keys tokens per user account or per requested scope set accumulates one dictionary entry and semaphore per key ever used for the lifetime of the OAuthClient.

## Suggested fix
Hold the in-flight refresh task per key and remove the entry when it completes (this also gives the shared-failure behaviour of mw-runtime-06), or remove the guard together with the token.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Per-key refresh state is removed when the refresh completes or the token is removed
- [ ] The number of retained guards stays constant after N distinct keys have been refreshed
- [ ] A a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Auth] OAuthClient refresh gate serializes failed refreshes so every waiter repeats the token request
body:
## Summary
RefreshTokenAsync serializes callers with a per-key semaphore and records nothing on failure, so each waiter finds the same expired token and sends its own token request. The wait before dispatch is not covered by the request timeout. With an unreachable token endpoint, twenty requests perform twenty sequential 30 s attempts, and rotating refresh tokens are presented repeatedly.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:166`

## Problem
RefreshTokenAsync takes a per-key SemaphoreSlim (OAuthClient.cs:164-166), re-checks the store (170-172) and sends the token request (184); on any failure it releases the gate (218-221) with nothing recorded, so the next waiter finds the same expired token and sends its own request. Waiters are bounded only by their caller token (`gate.WaitAsync(ct)`). AuthInterceptor awaits the provider before dispatch (AuthInterceptor.cs:65) with the caller token; request.Timeout is applied only by the transport (RawSocketTransport.cs:439-440), which has not started yet. OAuthClientTests.Refresh_SingleFlight (OAuthClientTests.cs:111-161) covers concurrent success only.

**Failure scenario.** The token endpoint is unreachable (each attempt runs to the 30 s default timeout). Twenty API requests are sent with an expired token: they queue on the gate and perform twenty sequential refresh attempts; the last one fails after about ten minutes although its own Timeout is 30 s, and every new request joins the queue. With rotating refresh tokens the repeated attempts also present the same refresh token again.

## Suggested fix
Make the refresh single-flight per key by sharing the in-flight Task<OAuthToken> (waiters await its result or its failure, optionally with a short failure hold-off) instead of a mutex around independent attempts, and bound the provider wait in AuthInterceptor by the request timeout.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Concurrent refreshes for one key share a single in-flight Task<OAuthToken>, and waiters observe its result or failure
- [ ] After a failed refresh waiters do not issue their own token request
- [ ] The provider wait in AuthInterceptor is bounded by the request timeout
- [ ] A a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-runtime-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. RefreshTokenAsync takes a per-key SemaphoreSlim (OAuthClient.cs:164-166), re-checks the store (170-172), sends (184) and releases in finally (218-221); a failure records nothing, so the next waiter finds the same expired token and sends again. Waiters are bounded only by `gate.WaitAsync(ct)` with the caller token. AuthInterceptor awaits the provider before dispatch (AuthInterceptor.cs:65) and the request timeout is created only inside the transport (RawSocketTransport.cs:439-441), so a queued request can wait N x token-request timeout regardless of its own Timeout. OAuthClientTests.Refresh_SingleFlight (111) is the only concurrency test and covers success. Needs a token endpoint that hangs rather than fails fast, so it is an edge case: medium.

title: [Auth] A rejected token cannot be refreshed: no 401 handling, no invalidate hook, and RefreshTokenAsync returns the stored token while not locally expired
body:
## Summary
RefreshTokenAsync returns the stored token whenever the local clock says it is unexpired, so an explicit refresh cannot reach the token endpoint. AuthInterceptor never looks at the response and IAuthTokenProvider has only GetTokenAsync. A revoked token or a clock set back causes 401 on every request until local expiry.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:171`

## Problem
RefreshTokenAsync first reads the store and returns `existing` whenever `!existing.IsExpired(_utcNow(), _defaultRefreshSkew)` (OAuthClient.cs:170-172); this is the de-duplication of concurrent refreshes, but it cannot tell 'another caller already refreshed' from 'the caller wants a refresh now'. Expiry is decided only from the local clock (OAuthToken.cs:35-38, OAuthClient.cs:264). AuthInterceptor passes the request on and never looks at the response (AuthInterceptor.cs:57-95); IAuthTokenProvider has a single GetTokenAsync (IAuthTokenProvider.cs:10-17). Core.Internal.AuthChallengeParser exists but is used only for proxy 407 (RawSocketTransport.cs:1710-1714).

**Failure scenario.** The server revokes the access token, or the device clock is set back after the token was issued (manual change, time correction on resume, token restored from persistent storage). Every request gets 401 until the local clock passes ExpiresAtUtc; calling RefreshTokenAsync explicitly returns the same rejected token without contacting the token endpoint. The only recovery is RemoveAsync on the app's own ITokenStore, which is impossible with the default store (mw-design-16).

## Spec reference
RFC 6750 section 3.1

## Suggested fix
Make the de-duplication compare tokens instead of clocks (skip the refresh only when the stored token differs from the one the caller holds), add an explicit force/invalidate entry point, and give AuthInterceptor an opt-in single retry on 401 that invalidates through the provider.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] De-duplication compares the stored token with the one the caller holds instead of using the clock
- [ ] An explicit force or invalidate entry point refreshes through the token endpoint
- [ ] AuthInterceptor offers an opt-in single retry on 401 that invalidates through the provider
- [ ] A a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-design-13` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. RefreshTokenAsync returns the stored token whenever it is not locally expired (Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:170-172) before building the refresh form, so an explicit refresh call cannot force a token-endpoint round trip; expiry is local wall clock only (OAuthToken.cs:35-38, OAuthClient.cs:264, default clock DateTime.UtcNow at OAuthClient.cs:38). AuthInterceptor never inspects the response (AuthInterceptor.cs:57-95), IAuthTokenProvider has only GetTokenAsync (IAuthTokenProvider.cs:16), and rg finds no 401/Unauthorized handling in Runtime/Auth or Runtime/Retry. Tests only cover single-flight (OAuthClientTests.cs:111) and invalid_grant. Correction to the scenario: recovery is possible in the documented setup, because the app owns the ITokenStore (Documentation~/Modules/Auth.md keeps `Store`) and can call RemoveAsync/SetAsync(key, null) (ITokenStore.cs:34-55); then existing == null and the refresh proceeds. So it is a missing feature plus an API trap (RefreshTokenAsync silently no-ops) rather than an unrecoverable state; the 401-until-local-expiry behaviour after revocation or a clock set-back holds by default. No open issue tracks it.

Related: [[R11-mw-design-16]].

title: [Auth] OAuthClient.RefreshTokenAsync posts the refresh token captured before the gate, so a rotated token can be replayed
body:
## Summary
GetValidTokenAsync copies the stored RefreshToken into the request before the single-flight gate and RefreshTokenAsync uses request.RefreshToken inside it. When another caller has already refreshed and the new access token is inside the skew, the second caller presents the old rotated refresh token. Providers with reuse detection revoke the token family and force a new login.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:177`

## Problem
GetValidTokenAsync reads the stored token and copies its RefreshToken into the request before the gate (OAuthClient.cs:260-273). Inside the gate RefreshTokenAsync re-reads `existing` only to decide whether it is still fresh (170-172); when it is not, the form uses `request.RefreshToken` (177), never `existing.RefreshToken`. Refresh_SingleFlight covers the case where the first refresh returns a token that is fresh by the skew.

**Failure scenario.** Access tokens live no longer than the refresh skew (default 60 s, or a larger custom skew) and the provider rotates refresh tokens. Callers A and B both read T1/R1; A refreshes and stores T2/R2; B enters the gate, finds T2 already inside the skew and posts R1 again. Providers with reuse detection revoke the token family: B gets invalid_grant, the stored token is removed (193) and the user must log in again.

## Spec reference
RFC 6749 section 6; RFC 9700 section 4.14

## Suggested fix
Inside the gate prefer `existing.RefreshToken` when a stored token exists, falling back to the request's value only when the store is empty.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Inside the gate the refresh uses the stored token's RefreshToken, falling back to the request value only when the store is empty
- [ ] A concurrent refresh with a rotating provider never presents a rotated-out refresh token
- [ ] A a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Auth] OAuth failures have no typed error and invalid_grant is detected by substring search
body:
## Summary
Refresh failures are InvalidOperationException (wrapped to UHttpErrorType.Unknown in a pipeline), the RFC 6749 error and error_description are discarded, and invalid_grant is matched by IndexOf on the raw body. An app must match an English message to show a login screen, and a 400 whose description mentions invalid_grant deletes the stored token.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:190`

## Problem
RefreshTokenAsync detects reauthorization with `body.IndexOf("invalid_grant", OrdinalIgnoreCase) >= 0` on the raw 400 body and throws InvalidOperationException("Refresh token invalid. Reauthorization is required.") (OAuthClient.cs:187-195); other non-success responses go to EnsureSuccessStatusCode, which throws UHttpException(HttpError) without the error/error_description fields (OAuthClient.cs:141, 197; UHttpResponse.cs:234-248). ParseTokenResponse and the OIDC checks throw InvalidOperationException (OAuthClient.cs:336, 341, 347, 506, 520). When this runs inside AuthInterceptor via OAuthTokenProvider, UHttpClient wraps any non-UHttp exception as UHttpException(Unknown, ex.Message, ex) (UHttpClient.cs:429-434). AuthInterceptor adds its own ArgumentException for CR/LF in the token (AuthInterceptor.cs:70-71), which UHttpRequest.WithHeader already checks (UHttpRequest.cs:177-179).

**Failure scenario.** The refresh token is revoked. Every API call fails with UHttpErrorType.Unknown and the message "Refresh token invalid..."; to show the login screen the app must match that English string or probe InnerException types. A 400 whose error_description merely mentions invalid_grant (for another error code) deletes the stored token.

## Spec reference
RFC 6749 section 5.2

## Suggested fix
Introduce one OAuth exception type carrying the parsed `error` and `error_description` and a 'reauthorization required' flag, parse the error object instead of searching the body, and map it to a defined UHttpErrorType when it crosses the pipeline.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A single OAuth exception type carries the parsed error, error_description and a reauthorization-required flag
- [ ] The error object is parsed, not searched, and only error=invalid_grant removes the stored token
- [ ] The exception maps to a defined UHttpErrorType when it crosses the pipeline
- [ ] A a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-design-15` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: invalid_grant is detected by body.IndexOf on a 400 and reported as InvalidOperationException after removing the stored token (Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:187-195); other failures go to EnsureSuccessStatusCode, which throws UHttpException(HttpError) with only the status (UHttpResponse.cs:234-248); parse/OIDC failures are InvalidOperationException (OAuthClient.cs:336, 341, 347, 506, 520); inside the pipeline UHttpClient wraps non-UHttp exceptions as Unknown with the original as inner (UHttpClient.cs:429-434). The substring match would also delete the token for a 400 whose error_description mentions invalid_grant. Correction to the failure scenario: not every call fails with Unknown. After the first failure the token is removed, GetValidTokenAsync returns null (OAuthClient.cs:260-262), OAuthTokenProvider returns null (OAuthTokenProvider.cs:40) and AuthInterceptor passes requests through unauthenticated (AuthInterceptor.cs:68), so later calls get the API's 401; only the first call and callers already queued on the gate (which re-send the revoked refresh token, since existing == null at line 171) see the Unknown error. Also a token-endpoint 4xx/5xx surfaces through the provider as UHttpException(HttpError) carrying the token endpoint's status on an API request. API-design debt (no typed OAuth error, RFC 6749 5.2 body dropped), functionally recoverable; the redundant CR/LF check at AuthInterceptor.cs:70-71 is harmless.

title: [Auth] Cancellation between the token response and the store write loses a rotated refresh token
body:
## Summary
RefreshTokenAsync writes the refreshed token with the caller's cancellation token, and InMemoryTokenStore.SetAsync throws on a cancelled token. If the request is cancelled or times out after the provider rotated the refresh token, the store keeps the old pair and the next refresh gets invalid_grant. The invalid_grant removal path has the same pattern.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:215`

## Problem
RefreshTokenAsync awaits `_tokenStore.SetAsync(key, token, ct)` with the caller's token (215), and InMemoryTokenStore.SetAsync starts with ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested() (ITokenStore.cs:36). The token comes from AuthInterceptor's per-request cancellationToken (AuthInterceptor.cs:65 -> OAuthTokenProvider.GetTokenAsync -> GetValidTokenAsync -> RefreshTokenAsync). The invalid_grant path has the same pattern with RemoveAsync (193).

**Failure scenario.** The request that triggered a refresh is cancelled or times out just as the token response is parsed: the provider has already rotated the refresh token, SetAsync throws OperationCanceledException, the store keeps the old pair, and the next refresh presents an invalidated refresh token -> invalid_grant -> forced re-login.

## Spec reference
RFC 6749 section 6

## Suggested fix
Persist the refreshed token (and the invalid_grant removal) with CancellationToken.None once the token response has been received.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The refreshed token and the invalid_grant removal are persisted with CancellationToken.None once the token response has been received
- [ ] Cancelling after the response leaves the new token in the store

title: [Auth] OAuthClient default token store is unreachable, ExchangeCodeAsync does not store its token, and GetValidTokenAsync mutates the caller's request
body:
## Summary
new OAuthClient() creates a private InMemoryTokenStore with no accessor, and ExchangeCodeAsync returns the token without storing it, so OAuthTokenProvider returns null and AuthInterceptor silently skips authentication. GetValidTokenAsync also returns an expired token and overwrites RefreshToken and TokenStoreKey on the caller's OAuthRefreshRequest, which architecture.md forbids.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:267`

## Problem
The constructor creates a private InMemoryTokenStore when none is passed and exposes no accessor (OAuthClient.cs:37); ExchangeCodeAsync returns the parsed token without SetAsync (OAuthClient.cs:139-145), unlike RefreshTokenAsync (215), so with `new OAuthClient()` GetValidTokenAsync always finds null and OAuthTokenProvider returns null, which AuthInterceptor treats as 'skip authentication' (AuthInterceptor.cs:68). Dispose does not dispose the store it created (302-313). GetValidTokenAsync returns the expired token when no refresh is possible (267-268) and overwrites refreshRequest.RefreshToken and TokenStoreKey on the caller's object (270-271), which architecture.md:112-114 names as forbidden; OAuthTokenProvider works around it by allocating a copy of the template per request (OAuthTokenProvider.cs:28-36), and the template's RefreshToken and TokenStoreKey it copies are always overwritten, so those two inputs are dead.

**Failure scenario.** new OAuthClient() + ExchangeCodeAsync + new AuthInterceptor(new OAuthTokenProvider(oauth, key)): requests go out unauthenticated with no error. A caller that reuses one OAuthRefreshRequest for two store keys gets the second key's refresh run with the first key's token store key and refresh token.

## Suggested fix
Store the exchanged token under a caller-supplied key (or expose the store), fail or return null instead of handing out an expired token from a method named GetValid, and build the effective refresh request internally instead of writing to the caller's object.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The exchanged token is stored under a caller-supplied key, or the store is exposed
- [ ] GetValidTokenAsync does not return an expired token as valid and does not modify the caller's request object
- [ ] The default store is disposed with the client

title: [Auth] OAuthClient.GetValidTokenAsync returns an expired token it cannot refresh; RefreshTokenAsync cannot force a refresh
body:
## Summary
GetValidTokenAsync returns the stored token unchanged when it is expired but no refresh request or refresh token is available, and OAuthTokenProvider then attaches the expired access token to every request. RefreshTokenAsync also returns the stored token whenever the clock says it is still valid, so a caller cannot force a refresh after the server rejected a revoked but unexpired token. Applications using a provider without a refresh template or handling 401 invalid_token are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:267`

## Problem
After finding the token expired (264), GetValidTokenAsync returns it unchanged when `refreshRequest == null` or the token has no refresh token (267-268). OAuthTokenProvider.GetTokenAsync returns `token?.AccessToken` (OAuthTokenProvider.cs:38-40) and AuthInterceptor sends it. RefreshTokenAsync also returns the stored token whenever it is not expired by the clock (171-172), so there is no way to force a refresh after the server rejected a token early.

**Failure scenario.** A provider built without a refresh template keeps sending `Authorization: Bearer <expired>` on every request; the method name says the result is valid, so callers do not check IsTokenExpired. After a 401 `invalid_token` for a revoked but unexpired token, calling RefreshTokenAsync returns the same rejected token.

## Spec reference
RFC 6750 section 3.1

## Suggested fix
Return null (or throw a typed error) for an expired token that cannot be refreshed, and give RefreshTokenAsync a way to bypass the freshness short-cut (for example compare the stored access token with the rejected one).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] GetValidTokenAsync returns null or throws a typed error for an expired token that cannot be refreshed, and OAuthTokenProvider does not send an expired access token
- [ ] RefreshTokenAsync can bypass the freshness short-cut, for example by comparing the stored access token with the rejected one, so a rejected unexpired token is replaced
- [ ] XML docs state the new contract
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Auth] OAuthClient.GetValidTokenAsync mutates the caller's OAuthRefreshRequest, mixing refresh tokens across keys
body:
## Summary
GetValidTokenAsync writes RefreshToken and TokenStoreKey into the OAuthRefreshRequest passed by the caller, and RefreshTokenAsync reads those fields again after awaits. Two concurrent calls for different keys that share one request object can overwrite each other, so one call posts the other user's refresh token and stores the result under the wrong key. This violates the documented rule that OAuthClient must not edit the caller's config.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:270`

## Problem
GetValidTokenAsync sets `refreshRequest.RefreshToken = token.RefreshToken; refreshRequest.TokenStoreKey = key;` on the caller's object (OAuthClient.cs:270-271). RefreshTokenAsync computes `key` before its first await (161-163) but reads `request.RefreshToken` and `request.Scope` after `gate.WaitAsync` and the store read (177, 181-182, 209). OAuthTokenProvider copies its template per call (OAuthTokenProvider.cs:28-36), which shows the hazard is known, but the public method itself is unguarded; OAuthClientTests.Refresh_SingleFlight (OAuthClientTests.cs:149-155) passes one request object to three concurrent calls (same key, so it does not show). architecture.md: 'OAuthClient must not edit the caller's config'.

**Failure scenario.** An app holds one OAuthRefreshRequest and calls GetValidTokenAsync("userA", shared) and GetValidTokenAsync("userB", shared) concurrently with both tokens expired: call B overwrites RefreshToken while call A is waiting on its gate; A then posts B's refresh token and stores the resulting token under userA's key.

## Suggested fix
Do not mutate the argument: copy the request (or pass key and refresh token as locals) in GetValidTokenAsync, and snapshot the request fields at the top of RefreshTokenAsync.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] GetValidTokenAsync does not modify the caller's OAuthRefreshRequest; key and refresh token are passed as locals or a copy is used
- [ ] RefreshTokenAsync snapshots the request fields before its first await
- [ ] Concurrent calls for userA and userB with one shared request each refresh with their own refresh token and store under their own key
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Auth] OAuthClient token and discovery requests follow 307/308 redirects and replay the code or refresh token cross-origin
body:
## Summary
OAuthClient sends token-endpoint and discovery requests through the application's UHttpClient with the default FollowRedirects=true. RedirectInterceptor keeps method and body on 307/308 and strips only Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization on a cross-origin hop, so the form body with the authorization code, code_verifier or refresh token is replayed to the redirect target. A misconfigured or compromised token endpoint host can collect credentials.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:321`

## Problem
SendTokenRequestAsync (315-331) and DiscoverAsync (234-237) send through the application's UHttpClient and set only the skip-auth metadata; the client's default FollowRedirects=true is applied (UHttpClient.cs:749). RedirectInterceptor preserves method and body for 307/308 and strips only Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization on a cross-origin hop (RedirectInterceptor.cs:133-138, 242-254), so the form body with `code`, `code_verifier` or `refresh_token` is replayed. ValidateDiscoveredIssuer checks against the requested discovery URL, not the final one.

**Failure scenario.** The token endpoint host (or a reverse proxy in front of it) answers the refresh POST with `307 Location: https://other.example/collect`: the client posts the refresh token to that origin and parses whatever JSON it returns as the new token.

## Spec reference
RFC 6749 sections 3.2, 10.3

## Suggested fix
Set RequestMetadataKeys.FollowRedirects=false on token-endpoint requests (a redirect there is an error) and on discovery, or restrict discovery redirects to the same origin.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Token-endpoint requests set RequestMetadataKeys.FollowRedirects=false and a redirect response is reported as an error
- [ ] Discovery requests do not follow redirects, or follow them only within the same origin as the discovery URL
- [ ] A test with a token endpoint answering 307 to another origin shows no request reaches that origin and the call fails with a typed error
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Auth] OAuth responses are parsed via ProjectJsonBridge and the app serializer; a missing bridge is found after the request
body:
## Summary
OAuthClient parses RFC 6749 token and discovery responses with ProjectJsonBridge, which forwards to the replaceable JsonSerializer.Default, so parsing depends on the application serializer supporting Dictionary<string, object>. A missing bridge registration is discovered only after the authorization_code POST was sent, so the single-use code is consumed and the user must log in again. architecture.md line 37 still describes the old reflection path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:435`

## Problem
DeserializeToDictionary calls ProjectJsonBridge.Deserialize(json, typeof(Dictionary<string, object>), ...) (OAuthClient.cs:435-442). The registered bridge forwards to JsonSerializer.Deserialize, which uses the replaceable default serializer (JsonModuleRegistration.cs:32-37, JsonSerializer.cs:117-120); TurboHttpBootstrap installs JsonUtilitySerializer and applications are told to call JsonSerializer.SetDefault with their own. So parsing of an RFC 6749 token response depends on the app serializer supporting Dictionary<string, object> with primitive boxing; GetNumber/GetString then guess at int/long/double/ToString (OAuthClient.cs:463-486). Nothing checks ProjectJsonBridge.IsRegistered before SendTokenRequestAsync (OAuthClient.cs:139-143, 184-200). The reflection of #67 is gone (ProjectJsonBridge.cs:11-13), but architecture.md:37 still describes it as reflection.

**Failure scenario.** A project sets a System.Text.Json source-generated or MessagePack-style IJsonSerializer that has no Dictionary<string, object> contract: every token exchange and refresh fails with "Failed to deserialize JSON payload for OAuth token parsing". A build without TurboHTTP.Complete that forgot JsonModuleRegistration.EnsureRegistered sends the authorization_code POST, the server consumes the single-use code, and only then does parsing throw; the user must log in again.

## Spec reference
RFC 6749 section 5.1

## Suggested fix
Parse the flat token/discovery object inside Auth with a fixed parser (a few dozen lines, or a Core.Internal flat-object reader shared with other modules) so Auth has no JSON dependency at all; failing that, check the bridge before any request is sent and bind the bridge to the built-in LiteJson rather than to the app's default serializer. Update architecture.md line 37.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Token and discovery responses are parsed by a fixed parser inside Auth (or a bound built-in LiteJson), independent of JsonSerializer.SetDefault
- [ ] If a bridge is still needed, its presence is checked before any token request is sent
- [ ] architecture.md line 37 is updated
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-design-14` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: DeserializeToDictionary goes through ProjectJsonBridge.Deserialize(typeof(Dictionary<string, object>)) (Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:435-442); the registered bridge forwards to JsonSerializer.Deserialize, i.e. the replaceable default (Runtime/JSON/JsonModuleRegistration.cs:32-37, JsonSerializer.cs:117-120). The bridge is only looked up inside ParseTokenResponse after SendTokenRequestAsync returned (OAuthClient.cs:139-143, 184-200; ProjectJsonBridge.cs:45-57 throws when unregistered), so an unregistered bridge is discovered after the authorization code was spent. architecture.md:37 still says 'through reflection' although ProjectJsonBridge.cs:11-13 is registration based. Mitigations that lower severity: the default bootstrap serializer routes Dictionary<string, object> to LiteJson (Runtime/Bootstrap/JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:37-40, 108-109), the documented Newtonsoft adapter yields string/long/double which GetString/GetNumber handle (OAuthClient.cs:463-486), and JsonElement.ToString() also works; the failure needs a custom serializer without a Dictionary<string, object> contract, or a build without TurboHTTP.Complete that skipped JsonModuleRegistration.EnsureRegistered (documented at ProjectJsonBridge.cs:8-10). Both fail deterministically on the first login in development, with a clear message. Real coupling/ordering weakness and a stale doc line, low impact.

title: [Auth] OAuthClient generates an OIDC nonce but never validates the id_token (iss, aud, exp, nonce)
body:
## Summary
CreateAuthorizationRequestAsync adds a nonce for the openid scope, but ExchangeCodeAsync only checks that an id_token string is present. OAuthCodeExchangeRequest has no nonce field, and OAuthToken.IdToken is returned as an opaque string. OpenID Connect Core 3.1.3.7 requires the client to validate iss, aud, exp and the nonce, so an application that trusts the id_token because the library required it can accept a replayed or substituted token.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:497`

## Problem
CreateAuthorizationRequestAsync adds a nonce when the scope contains `openid` (53, 72-73) and returns it in OAuthAuthorizationRequest. ExchangeCodeAsync only verifies that an id_token string is present (ValidateOidcTokenPresence 497-507); OAuthCodeExchangeRequest has no nonce field and the token is returned as an opaque string (OAuthToken.IdToken). OpenID Connect Core section 3.1.3.7 requires the client to validate iss, aud, exp and the nonce it sent.

**Failure scenario.** An application uses the `openid` scope, trusts `token.IdToken` for the user's identity because the library 'required' it, and never compares the nonce: a replayed or substituted id_token from another session or client is accepted.

## Spec reference
OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 3.1.3.7

## Suggested fix
Either validate the id_token claims that need no signature key (iss against the discovered issuer, aud == client_id, exp, nonce passed in OAuthCodeExchangeRequest), or document on OAuthToken.IdToken and OAuthAuthorizationRequest.Nonce that validation is the caller's duty.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ExchangeCodeAsync validates the claims that need no signature key (iss against the discovered issuer, aud equals client_id, exp, nonce supplied via OAuthCodeExchangeRequest), or XML docs on OAuthToken.IdToken and OAuthAuthorizationRequest.Nonce state that validation is the caller's duty
- [ ] A mismatching nonce, iss, aud or an expired id_token is rejected with a typed error when validation is implemented
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Auth] OIDC discovery skips issuer validation when issuer is missing and compares it after URI normalization
body:
## Summary
ValidateDiscoveredIssuer returns without checking when the discovery document has no absolute issuer value, although OpenID Connect Discovery makes issuer required and identical to the URL the configuration was fetched for. The comparison also normalizes host case, default port and trailing slash instead of comparing exactly. A document that omits issuer but points its endpoints at another host is accepted and replaces the configured endpoints.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:511`

## Problem
ValidateDiscoveredIssuer returns when `issuer == null` (OAuthClient.cs:511-512); CreateUriIfPresent yields null for a missing or non-absolute value (488-495). OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 section 3 makes `issuer` REQUIRED and section 4.3 requires it to be identical to the URL the configuration was fetched for. AreEquivalentIssuers compares UriBuilder-normalized strings (548-568): host case, default port and trailing slash are ignored. OAuthClientTests.Discovery_IssuerMismatch_IsRejected covers only a present, different issuer.

**Failure scenario.** A discovery document without `issuer` (or with `issuer: "x"`) but with authorization_endpoint/token_endpoint on another host is accepted and its endpoints replace the configured ones; the check meant to detect a wrong or mixed-up provider is bypassed by omitting the field.

## Spec reference
OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 sections 3, 4.3

## Suggested fix
Fail discovery when `issuer` is missing or not an absolute https URL, and compare it to the expected issuer string exactly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Discovery fails with a typed error when issuer is missing or is not an absolute https URL
- [ ] Issuer is compared to the expected issuer string exactly, without URI normalization
- [ ] Tests cover a missing issuer, a non-URL issuer and a differently normalized issuer
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Auth] StaticTokenProvider, OAuthTokenProvider and AuthInterceptor allocate per request for unchanging values
body:
## Summary
StaticTokenProvider creates a new Task per call, OAuthTokenProvider builds an OAuthRefreshRequest before knowing whether a refresh is needed and goes through three async state machines, and AuthInterceptor concatenates the scheme and token on every request. Every authenticated request allocates a Task<string> plus the header string, and about 300-400 B more with the OAuth provider while the token is valid.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/StaticTokenProvider.cs:25`

## Problem
StaticTokenProvider.GetTokenAsync returns `Task.FromResult(_token)` on every call (StaticTokenProvider.cs:25). OAuthTokenProvider.GetTokenAsync builds a new OAuthRefreshRequest before knowing whether a refresh is needed (OAuthTokenProvider.cs:28-36) and awaits OAuthClient.GetValidTokenAsync, which awaits InMemoryTokenStore.GetAsync (another Task.FromResult, ITokenStore.cs:27-32). AuthInterceptor concatenates scheme and token for each request (AuthInterceptor.cs:74, 130-136) and reads/writes the origin in the context state under its lock (118-123).

**Failure scenario.** Every authenticated request allocates a Task<string> plus the header string with a static token, and about 300-400 B more (request object, two state machines, a store task) with the OAuth provider while the token is still valid.

## Suggested fix
Cache the completed Task<string> in StaticTokenProvider; in OAuthTokenProvider read the store first and build the refresh request only when the token is expired; cache the last (token, header value) pair in AuthInterceptor.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] StaticTokenProvider returns a cached completed Task<string>
- [ ] OAuthTokenProvider reads the store first and builds the refresh request only when the token is expired
- [ ] AuthInterceptor caches the last (token, header value) pair
- [ ] An allocation test shows zero managed allocations per request for a static token and a valid OAuth token after warm-up, under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/

title: [Middleware] Disposing CookieJar races in-flight requests and CookieHandler fails responses on a disposed jar
body:
## Summary
CookieJar.Dispose disposes its ReaderWriterLockSlim without excluding threads that are inside or about to enter the lock. CookieHandler.OnResponseStartAsync calls StoreSetCookies unguarded, so a response arriving after dispose throws ObjectDisposedException and the transport reports an Unknown error for a response that was received intact. Dispose itself can throw SynchronizationLockException when a writer is waiting. The redirect-observer paths already drop cookies instead of failing.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieHandler.cs:41`

## Problem
CookieJar.Dispose (CookieJar.cs:354-360) sets `_disposed` and disposes `_lock` without excluding threads that are between ThrowIfDisposed and Enter*Lock or inside the lock; ReaderWriterLockSlim.Dispose throws SynchronizationLockException when another thread is waiting on it. UHttpClient.Dispose disposes IDisposable interceptors while requests may still be in flight (architecture.md 'Request pipeline'). The redirect-observer paths swallow ObjectDisposedException on purpose (CookieInterceptor.cs:207-216, 235-242: 'drop the cookies rather than failing the redirect hop'), but CookieHandler.OnResponseStartAsync calls StoreSetCookies unguarded (CookieHandler.cs:41, 50-59), so the ObjectDisposedException leaves the handler callback before the body is forwarded.

**Failure scenario.** A scene unload disposes the client while a request is in flight; its response carries Set-Cookie: the handler callback throws ObjectDisposedException, the transport aborts the body and reports an Unknown error for a response that was received intact. If a writer is waiting on the lock at that moment, Dispose itself throws SynchronizationLockException out of UHttpClient.Dispose.

## Suggested fix
Use a plain `lock` (short critical sections, nothing to dispose) or keep the lock alive and only flip `_disposed`; treat a disposed jar in CookieHandler like the observer paths do.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Disposing the jar while a response with Set-Cookie arrives does not fail the response; cookies are dropped
- [ ] CookieJar.Dispose never throws SynchronizationLockException
- [ ] CookieHandler treats a disposed jar like the redirect observers do
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Middleware] Cookie, DefaultHeaders and Auth interceptors skip the documented request-rewrite restore/cleanup contract
body:
## Summary
architecture.md requires an interceptor that rewrites a request to copy it, update the context, restore the original in finally and dispose the copy if next() fails. Only DecompressionInterceptor does this; CookieInterceptor, DefaultHeadersInterceptor and AuthInterceptor wrap only the synchronous call to next in try/catch and await the task outside it, so their cleanup is unreachable for async failures. context.Request can then describe a request that was not sent, for example after a retry where the second attempt made no copy.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieInterceptor.cs:82`

## Problem
architecture.md:98-101 states that an interceptor that rewrites a request copies it, calls context.UpdateRequest, restores the original in finally and disposes the copy if next() throws. DecompressionInterceptor does this (DecompressionInterceptor.cs:75-94: catch around the awaited call, finally restores). CookieInterceptor (CookieInterceptor.cs:82-102), DefaultHeadersInterceptor (DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:56-72) and AuthInterceptor (AuthInterceptor.cs:78-94) wrap only the synchronous call `next(...)` in try/catch and then `await dispatchTask` outside it. `next` is normally an async lambda, which never throws synchronously, so their restore/dispose code is unreachable for almost every failure and never runs on success. RedirectHandler also leaves the last hop request on the context (RedirectHandler.cs:237).

**Failure scenario.** With DecompressionInterceptor outermost, context.Request after the dispatch is the caller's request; with Cookie or Auth outermost it is their private copy (with the Cookie/Authorization header). A RetryInterceptor outside AuthInterceptor: attempt 1 attaches token A and updates the context; on attempt 2 the provider returns null, no copy is made, and context.Request still shows attempt 1's copy with token A, so handlers that read the context at body end (logging, monitor, #70) describe a request that was not sent.

## Suggested fix
Extract the copy/update/restore/dispose sequence into one Core helper (it is the same primitive #76 asks to make public) and use it in all four interceptors, with the await inside the try. Decide once whether redirect hops should stay on the context and document it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Copy/update/restore/dispose is implemented once in a Core helper and used by Cookie, DefaultHeaders, Auth and Decompression interceptors with the await inside the try
- [ ] context.Request equals the caller's request after dispatch on success, failure and cancellation
- [ ] The decision whether redirect hops stay on the context is made and documented
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Middleware] CookieJar has no clear, remove, enumerate or persist API; sessions cannot end locally
body:
## Summary
The public surface of CookieJar is the constructor, Count, GetDomainCount, StoreFromSetCookieHeaders, GetCookieHeader and Dispose, and CookieInterceptor takes the concrete type. An application cannot drop a session cookie on logout without rebuilding the client, and cookies with Expires or Max-Age are parsed but never exportable, so a remember-me cookie is lost on every restart. A cookie from one account can carry over to the next.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:21`

## Problem
The public surface is the constructor, Count, GetDomainCount, StoreFromSetCookieHeaders, GetCookieHeader and Dispose (CookieJar.cs:158-360). CookieRecord is a private nested class (129-145), there is no interface, and CookieInterceptor takes the concrete type and holds it in a readonly field (CookieInterceptor.cs:26, 35-50). Interceptors are fixed when the client is constructed (architecture.md:41-43). Expires/Max-Age are parsed and stored (CookieJar.cs:474-505, 551) but no export or import exists.

**Failure scenario.** Logout: the app cannot drop the session cookie; it must dispose the client and build a new one with a new jar, or forge Set-Cookie deletions for names it cannot list. A mobile game with a 30-day 'remember me' cookie loses it on every app restart, and the app cannot implement persistence itself.

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 section 5.3

## Suggested fix

title: [Middleware] CookieJar is IDisposable only for its ReaderWriterLockSlim, forcing ownership and disposed-state handling
body:
## Summary
The jar's only disposable member is its ReaderWriterLockSlim, which makes CookieInterceptor implement IDisposable, track _ownsJar, and handle ObjectDisposedException in some paths but not in CookieInterceptor/CookieHandler main paths. The read lock gives little because GetCookieHeader re-takes the write lock whenever it sees an expired cookie. A client disposed while a response arrives reports a fully received response as failed.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:122`

## Problem
The jar's only disposable member is `_lock` (CookieJar.cs:122, 354-360). Because of it CookieInterceptor implements IDisposable and tracks `_ownsJar` (CookieInterceptor.cs:22, 27, 40-49, 257-264), every public jar method starts with ThrowIfDisposed, the redirect observers need ObjectDisposedException handlers (CookieInterceptor.cs:207-216, 235-242) while the main path has none (CookieInterceptor.cs:64, CookieHandler.cs:41), and UHttpClientOptions.DisposeInterceptors has to be reasoned about (#63). The read lock gives little: GetCookieHeader takes the write lock again whenever it saw an expired cookie (CookieJar.cs:338-349) and each read section is a short in-memory scan.

**Failure scenario.** A client with DisposeInterceptors = true is disposed while a response is arriving: CookieHandler.OnResponseStartAsync calls StoreFromSetCookieHeaders on the disposed jar, the ObjectDisposedException is turned into UHttpException(Unknown) and a response that was fully received is reported as failed.

## Suggested fix
Guard the dictionary with a plain lock, drop IDisposable from CookieJar and CookieInterceptor (keep no-op Dispose only if the public API must stay), and remove the disposed checks and handlers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The jar guards its dictionary with a plain lock and no longer needs disposal (a no-op Dispose is kept only if the public API requires it)
- [ ] The disposed checks, _ownsJar tracking and ObjectDisposedException handlers are removed

title: [Middleware] CookieJar resets a cookie's creation time on replacement, changing Cookie header order
body:
## Summary
StoreFromSetCookieHeaders overwrites the stored record with CreatedAtUtc set to now, but RFC 6265 section 5.3 step 11.3 requires the new cookie to keep the old cookie's creation time. Because GetCookieHeader orders equal-length paths by creation time, a cookie refreshed by the server moves behind others in the Cookie header. Servers that take the first of two same-named cookies can then read a different value than they do for browsers.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:253`

## Problem
StoreFromSetCookieHeaders overwrites the record (`_cookies[key] = cookie`, 253) with CreatedAtUtc = now (555). RFC 6265 section 5.3 step 11.3 copies the old cookie's creation-time to the new one, and GetCookieHeader orders equal-length paths by creation time (323-325) per section 5.4 step 2.

**Failure scenario.** Cookies `a` then `b` are set on `/`; the server refreshes `a` on every response. Browsers keep sending `a=..; b=..`; this jar switches to `b=..; a=..` after the first refresh, which breaks servers that take the first of two same-named cookies with different Domain scope.

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 sections 5.3 step 11.3, 5.4 step 2

## Suggested fix
Carry CreatedAtUtc over from the record being replaced.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Replacing an existing cookie keeps the old CreatedAtUtc
- [ ] GetCookieHeader orders cookies a then b after a is refreshed, as RFC 6265 section 5.4 step 2 requires
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Middleware] CookieJar.GetCookieHeader scans every stored cookie and allocates per request with no empty-jar fast path
body:
## Summary
GetCookieHeader takes the read lock, normalizes the host, allocates a match list and walks all stored cookies (up to 3000) for every request, even when the jar is empty. CookieInterceptor also registers redirect-observer state in the context on every request. Clients with large jars pay linear cost per request under a shared lock.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:290`

## Problem
GetCookieHeader (CookieJar.cs:264-352) takes the read lock, normalizes the host with Trim/TrimStart/ToLowerInvariant (286, 714-717), allocates `new List<CookieRecord>()` (290) and walks all of `_cookies.Values` (up to maxTotalCookies = 3000) doing domain and path matching per cookie (291-313); there is no index by domain and no early return when the jar is empty. A request that sees one expired cookie takes the write lock and runs RemoveExpiredUnsafe, which allocates another list and scans again (338-349, 647-658). CookieInterceptor.Wrap additionally does per request: GetState + SetState of the caller Cookie header, AddResponseObserver (two GetState, a new one-element array, SetState) and a CookieHandler (CookieInterceptor.cs:78-87; RedirectHandler.cs:87-109), each state call under the RequestContext lock, even when no RedirectInterceptor is in the pipeline.

**Failure scenario.** A client with a CookieInterceptor and a jar holding 2,000 cookies from many hosts (a browser-like or multi-tenant app) pays 2,000 domain/path comparisons under the shared lock for every request; with an empty jar each request still pays the list, the string normalization and five context-lock round trips.

## Suggested fix
Return null before any work when `_cookies.Count == 0`; index cookies by domain (Dictionary<string, List<CookieRecord>>) and probe only the host and its parent domains; allocate the match list lazily. In CookieInterceptor register the observer state once per context only when needed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] GetCookieHeader returns null without allocating when the jar holds no cookies
- [ ] Cookie lookup probes only the request host and its parent domains instead of scanning all cookies
- [ ] Allocations per request with an empty jar are measured and reduced to zero in the jar path
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Middleware] CookieJar stores cookie names and values with control characters, making later requests to that scope fail
body:
## Summary
TryParseSetCookie checks only for an empty name and the length limit, so a Set-Cookie containing C0 or DEL bytes is stored. The serializer then rejects the Cookie header, so every later request to that scope fails until the process restarts. A malicious or buggy server can lock the client out of a domain.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:382`

## Problem
TryParseSetCookie (CookieJar.cs:377-388) checks only for an empty name and the 4096 length. HTTP/1.1 response header values are not validated (Http11ResponseParser.ParseResponseHeaderLine 699-722: NUL, bare CR, other C0 and DEL pass); HTTP/2 rejects only NUL/CR/LF (Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:779). GetCookieHeader echoes the stored value (741-743). Outbound, UHttpRequest.WithHeader rejects CR/LF with ArgumentException (called at CookieInterceptor.cs:69 and 252) and HttpFieldValidator rejects every C0 control except HTAB and DEL (Transport/Internal/HttpFieldValidator.cs:84-91), mapped to UHttpException InvalidRequest (RawSocketTransport.cs:822). CookieJar has no public remove/clear API.

**Failure scenario.** `evil.example.com` (or an on-path attacker answering any http:// request for the domain) sends `Set-Cookie: x=a\x01b; Domain=example.com; Max-Age=315360000`. Every later request of this client to *.example.com fails before it is sent (`Header value for 'Cookie' contains control character 0x01`; with a bare CR an ArgumentException out of CookieInterceptor) until the process restarts. A server that emits such a byte by mistake locks itself out the same way.

## Spec reference
RFC 6265bis section 5.6; RFC 6265 section 4.1.1

## Suggested fix
Ignore a set-cookie-string whose name or value contains %x00-08, %x0A-1F or %x7F (RFC 6265bis section 5.6), so the jar never holds a cookie the serializer refuses; expose Clear/Remove on CookieJar.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A set-cookie-string whose name or value contains %x00-08, %x0A-1F or %x7F is ignored (RFC 6265bis section 5.6)
- [ ] The jar never holds a cookie that the Cookie header serializer refuses
- [ ] CookieJar exposes Clear and Remove so a bad state can be recovered without restart
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: TryParseSetCookie checks only an empty name and the 4096 length (CookieJar.cs:377-388). HTTP/1.1 response values are Latin-1 decoded and whitespace-trimmed with no control-character check (Http11ResponseParser.cs:699-722, DecodeLineFromBuffer :1515-1533; a bare CR inside a line survives), HTTP/2 rejects only NUL/CR/LF (Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:779). GetCookieHeader echoes the stored value (CookieJar.cs:741-743). Outbound: UHttpRequest.WithHeader throws ArgumentException on CR/LF (UHttpRequest.cs:577-583, called at CookieInterceptor.cs:69 and :252) and Http11RequestSerializer.cs:518 / Http2Connection.Send.cs:457 run HttpFieldValidator, which rejects C0 controls and DEL (HttpFieldValidator.cs:84-91) as InvalidRequest (RawSocketTransport.cs:822). CookieJar has no public remove/clear API, and the server cannot delete the cookie because no request to its scope is sent any more. A Domain cookie from one host poisons the whole registrable domain until expiry or eviction.

title: [Middleware] CookieJar strips surrounding double quotes from cookie values and returns a different value than the server set
body:
## Summary
TryParseSetCookie unquotes cookie values via UnquoteCookieValue, and GetCookieHeader sends the unquoted value. RFC 6265 makes the DQUOTEs part of cookie-value, so servers that quote values receive a different string back. An existing test asserts the wrong behaviour.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:383`

## Problem
TryParseSetCookie passes the value through UnquoteCookieValue (383, 787-796), which removes a leading and trailing DQUOTE; GetCookieHeader then sends the unquoted value (741-743). RFC 6265 section 5.2 has no unquoting step and section 4.1.1 makes the DQUOTEs part of cookie-value; browsers return them verbatim. Tests/Runtime/Middleware/CookieInterceptorTests.cs:452 (CookieJar_UnquotesCookieValues) asserts `token="abc"` is sent back as `token=abc`.

**Failure scenario.** A server sets `Set-Cookie: session="a\054b:sig"` (Python http.cookies and Tomcat's legacy cookie processor quote values with special characters and decode only quoted values). The client returns `session=a\054b:sig`; the server compares or decodes a different string and treats the session as invalid.

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 sections 4.1.1, 5.2

## Suggested fix
Store and return the value exactly as received after trimming WSP; delete UnquoteCookieValue and invert the test.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A cookie value received as "abc" is sent back as "abc" including the quotes
- [ ] UnquoteCookieValue is removed and CookieJar_UnquotesCookieValues in CookieInterceptorTests is inverted
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Middleware] CookieJar compares Uri.Host instead of the A-label host, so punycode Domain attributes never match Unicode IDN hosts
body:
## Summary
TryParseSetCookie and GetCookieHeader use requestUri.Host, which keeps U-labels for hosts written in Unicode, while servers send Domain in A-label form. The ordinal comparison fails and the cookie is rejected. Users of internationalized domain names lose their sessions.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:390`

## Problem
TryParseSetCookie and GetCookieHeader take `requestUri.Host` (390, 286), which keeps U-labels when the URL was written in Unicode; servers send `Domain=xn--...`. DomainMatches is an ordinal comparison (660-674). RFC 6265 section 5.1.2 canonicalizes hosts to A-labels; the transport already does this through WireHost.LookupHost (RawSocketTransport.cs:478).

**Failure scenario.** Request to `https://bücher.example/login`; the response sets `sid=1; Domain=xn--bcher-kva.example`: the Domain does not match `bücher.example`, the cookie is rejected and the session is lost. (Depends on Uri.Host returning the Unicode form on Unity's Mono; confirm there.)

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 section 5.1.2

## Suggested fix
Canonicalize the request host with Uri.IdnHost (or the Core WireHost helper) before matching and storing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Request host is canonicalized to A-labels (Uri.IdnHost or the Core WireHost helper) before storing and matching
- [ ] A cookie with Domain=xn--bcher-kva.example set by https://bücher.example is stored and sent back

title: [Middleware] CookieJar Set-Cookie attribute handling deviates from RFC 6265 5.2/5.3 for empty Domain, repeated Domain and Max-Age
body:
## Summary
An empty Domain attribute rejects the whole cookie, the first failing Domain returns immediately instead of the last Domain winning, and Max-Age<=0 is never cleared by a later valid Max-Age. Browsers handle all three per the RFC, so cookies from such servers are dropped or deleted wrongly.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:425`

## Problem
(a) `Domain=` or a bare `Domain` returns false for the whole cookie (425-426); section 5.2.3 says to ignore the attribute. (b) Attributes are applied in order and a Domain that fails the match returns immediately (447-448, 456-457), although section 5.3 step 3 uses the last Domain attribute. (c) `shouldDelete` is set by any `Max-Age<=0` and never cleared (493-497), so `Max-Age=0; Max-Age=3600` deletes; a later unparsable Max-Age also leaves an earlier one in force. (d) long.TryParse with AllowLeadingSign accepts `+5` (490), which section 5.2.2 rejects, and an all-digit value that overflows long is ignored instead of meaning the far future.

**Failure scenario.** A framework configured with an empty cookie domain emits `Set-Cookie: sid=abc; Domain=; Path=/`: browsers store a host-only cookie, this jar drops it and the login never sticks.

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 sections 5.2.2, 5.2.3, 5.3

## Suggested fix
Collect the last occurrence of each attribute first, then evaluate; treat an empty Domain as absent; parse Max-Age as `-?DIGIT+` with saturation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An empty or bare Domain attribute is ignored and the cookie becomes host-only
- [ ] The last occurrence of each attribute (Domain, Max-Age, Expires, Path) is the one evaluated
- [ ] Max-Age is parsed as -?DIGIT+ with saturation and a later valid Max-Age overrides an earlier one
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Middleware] CookieJar parses Expires with DateTime.TryParse instead of the RFC 6265 cookie-date algorithm
body:
## Summary
Expires is parsed with DateTime.TryParse, which rejects common cookie dates (UTC zone name, RFC 850 with a UTC zone, asctime, wrong weekday) and accepts non-cookie formats. A failed parse stores the cookie without expiry, so logout cookies with a 1970 Expires are kept and sent.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:476`

## Problem
CookieJar.cs:474-486 calls DateTime.TryParse(InvariantCulture, AdjustToUniversal | AssumeUniversal); on failure the attribute is ignored and the cookie is stored without expiry (253). Run with the same arguments on .NET 8: `Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 UTC` -> false, `Thursday, 01-Jan-1970 00:00:00 UTC` (PHP DATE_COOKIE under a UTC zone) -> false, asctime `Thu Jan  1 00:00:00 1970` -> false, a wrong weekday `Mon, 09 Jun 2021 10:18:14 GMT` -> false; `1/2/2030` and `2021-06-09T10:18:14Z` -> true, and `+0200` shifts the time although section 5.1.1 ignores weekday and zone tokens. Two-digit years follow Calendar.TwoDigitYearMax (2049 on .NET 8, 2029 on .NET Framework-derived libraries) instead of the 70-99 / 0-69 rule. The only Expires test uses one RFC 1123 date (CookieInterceptorTests.cs:149).

**Failure scenario.** Logout answers `Set-Cookie: sid=deleted; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 UTC`: the jar does not delete the cookie, stores `sid=deleted` as a session cookie and keeps sending it. A persistent cookie with an unparsed Expires silently never expires. If Unity's Mono pivots two-digit years at 2029, `Expires=Friday, 14-Nov-31 08:00:00 GMT` becomes 1931 and the cookie is dropped on receipt (needs a Unity run to confirm).

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 section 5.1.1

## Suggested fix
Implement the section 5.1.1 token algorithm (time, day-of-month, month, year tokens in any order; 70-99 -> 19xx, 0-69 -> 20xx; ignore everything else) and add table tests for RFC 1123, RFC 850, asctime, `UTC` and wrong-weekday inputs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Expires is parsed with the RFC 6265 section 5.1.1 token algorithm (time, day, month, year tokens in any order; 70-99 -> 19xx, 0-69 -> 20xx)
- [ ] Table tests cover RFC 1123, RFC 850, asctime, a UTC zone and a wrong weekday
- [ ] A 1970 Expires deletes an existing cookie
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

Re-ran the cited inputs on .NET 8 with the same arguments: 'Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 UTC' false, 'Thursday, 01-Jan-1970 00:00:00 UTC' false, asctime false, wrong weekday false; '1/2/2030' and ISO 8601 true; '+0200' shifts the time. RFC 850 with GMT and two-digit years parsed correctly on .NET 8 (31 -> 2031), so the two-digit-year scenario is unproven and depends on Unity Mono's TwoDigitYearMax (not run). title: [Middleware] CookieJar.EnforceLimitsUnsafe purges expired cookies with DateTime.UtcNow instead of the utcNowOverride
body:
## Summary
StoreFromSetCookieHeaders honours utcNowOverride for parsing and the first purge, but EnforceLimitsUnsafe calls RemoveExpiredUnsafe(DateTime.UtcNow). With an override in the past, a valid cookie is removed immediately. The public test-only parameter is also an API-shape smell.

- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:564`

StoreFromSetCookieHeaders resolves nowUtc from the optional utcNowOverride and uses it for parsing and the first purge (CookieJar.cs:224, 230, 238), then calls EnforceLimitsUnsafe, which calls RemoveExpiredUnsafe(DateTime.UtcNow) (CookieJar.cs:256, 564). **Failure scenario.** jar.StoreFromSetCookieHeaders(uri, new[] { "a=b; Max-Age=3600" }, utcNowOverride: yesterday) computes an expiry 23 hours ago; the limit pass removes the cookie immediately, and GetCookieHeader(uri, ..., utcNowOverride: yesterday + 1 minute) returns null although the cookie is valid at the overridden time.

Pass nowUtc into EnforceLimitsUnsafe, and move the clock to an internal constructor-injected Func<DateTime> so the public methods lose the test-only parameter.
