title: [Middleware] CookieJar.StoreFromSetCookieHeaders holds the write lock across parsing and the isPublicSuffix callback, with repeated full scans
body:
## Summary
Storing Set-Cookie takes the write lock and, inside it, runs an expiry sweep, parsing, the user callback, a shadow-cookie scan and limit enforcement with a second sweep. Eviction is O(evicted x total). A large response with a full jar blocks every concurrent GetCookieHeader.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:564`

## Problem
StoreFromSetCookieHeaders takes the write lock (CookieJar.cs:227) and inside it: RemoveExpiredUnsafe(nowUtc) (230: new List + full scan), TryParseSetCookie per line (238: Split(';'), Trim/Substring per attribute, DateTime.TryParse, the caller's isPublicSuffix delegate at 443/819), ShadowsSecureCookieUnsafe full scan per non-secure cookie from an http origin (243, 798-812), then EnforceLimitsUnsafe (256), which calls RemoveExpiredUnsafe again with DateTime.UtcNow instead of the method's nowUtc (564), builds a Dictionary of domain counts by scanning everything (566, 599-611) and copies its keys to a List (580). TryEvictOldestUnsafe scans the whole dictionary for each evicted cookie (613-645). All readers (every outbound request, GetCookieHeader's read lock) wait meanwhile.

**Failure scenario.** A response with 30 Set-Cookie lines arrives while the jar holds 3,000 cookies and is at its limit: about 3 full scans, 30 full eviction scans (90,000 record visits) and all parsing run under the write lock, blocking every concurrent request's GetCookieHeader. With a small jar the cost is the four allocations and three scans per Set-Cookie response.

## Suggested fix
Parse outside the lock and take the write lock only to apply the parsed records; skip the expiry sweep and limit enforcement when nothing can be over (Count <= min(limits) and no record expired), keep per-domain counts incrementally, and use the same `nowUtc` in EnforceLimitsUnsafe.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Set-Cookie lines are parsed outside the lock and the write lock only applies parsed records
- [ ] The expiry sweep and limit enforcement are skipped when nothing can be expired or over a limit
- [ ] The user-supplied isPublicSuffix delegate is never invoked under the jar lock
- [ ] Per-response allocations and record visits are measured and reduced for a 30-cookie response on a 3000-cookie jar

title: [Middleware] CookieJar enforces the total limit before the per-domain limit, so one site can evict every other site's cookies
body:
## Summary
Per-domain limits count by exact Domain value, and the global LRU eviction runs before the per-domain trim, the reverse of RFC 6265 section 5.3. A single response with many parent-domain cookies fills the jar and evicts other sites' cookies. The user is logged out everywhere.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:568`

## Problem
BuildDomainCountsUnsafe counts by `cookie.Domain` (599-611), so a.b.c.evil.com may store 50 cookies for each of a.b.c.evil.com, b.c.evil.com, c.evil.com and evil.com, and wildcard subdomains add 50 host-only cookies each. EnforceLimitsUnsafe runs the global LRU eviction (568-578) before the per-domain trim (580-596), the reverse of RFC 6265 section 5.3, so cookies of other sites are evicted to make room for cookies the per-domain pass removes right after. The response header limit (100 KB, Http11ResponseParser.cs:158) allows about 3000 short Set-Cookie lines.

**Failure scenario.** A response from a host with ~60 labels under evil.com sets 50 cookies for each parent domain (3000 cookies in ~100 KB): the jar is at its total limit, all less recently used cookies of every other site are gone, and the user is logged out everywhere.

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 sections 5.3, 6.1

## Suggested fix
Trim per domain before the global pass and count the per-domain limit by registrable domain (public suffix + 1, using the same predicate), or add a per-response cap.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Per-domain trimming runs before the global eviction pass
- [ ] The per-domain limit counts by registrable domain, or a per-response cap bounds the cookies a single response can add
- [ ] A response setting cookies for many parent domains does not evict cookies of unrelated sites

title: [Middleware] CookieJar accepts Domain=com. because a trailing dot defeats the public-suffix and single-label checks
body:
## Summary
NormalizeDomain trims only leading dots, and Uri.Host keeps a trailing dot, so Domain=com. set by evil.com. passes IsRejectedPublicSuffix. The cookie is then sent to every *.com. host, enabling session fixation across sites after an attacker redirect.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:827`

## Problem
NormalizeDomain (714-717) trims only leading dots, and Uri.Host keeps a trailing dot (`new Uri("http://evil.com./x").Host == "evil.com."`, checked on .NET 8). For `Domain=com.` IsRejectedPublicSuffix (822-842) splits into ["com", ""], so `labels.Length < 2` is false, the set lookup misses and `labels[1].Length == 2` is false; a PSL-backed isPublicSuffix predicate is also asked about `com.`. DomainMatches("evil.com.", "com.", false) is true (660-674), so the cookie is stored with Domain `com.` (459-461) and later matches `victim.com.`. The same holds for `co.uk.` and every entry of KnownMultiLabelPublicSuffixes. CookieJarScopingTests has no trailing-dot case.

**Failure scenario.** The client follows an attacker redirect: http://evil.com/ -> 302 http://evil.com./a, which answers `Set-Cookie: session=ATTACKER; Domain=com.` and `302 Location: https://victim.com./account`. The request to victim.com. carries `Cookie: session=ATTACKER` (session fixation / login CSRF against any site, and one cookie reaching every dotted .com host).

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 sections 5.1.2, 5.3 step 5

## Suggested fix
Canonicalize hosts and Domain values before every comparison (strip one trailing dot, or reject a Domain attribute that ends with a dot or contains an empty label) and treat an empty label as invalid in IsRejectedPublicSuffix. Add a regression case to CookieJarScopingTests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Host and Domain values are canonicalized (single trailing dot stripped) before every comparison, or a Domain ending in a dot or with an empty label is rejected
- [ ] IsRejectedPublicSuffix treats an empty label as invalid
- [ ] Regression cases for com. and co.uk. are added to CookieJarScopingTests
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

IsRejectedPublicSuffix splits into ['com',''] so labels.Length < 2 is false, the set lookup misses and labels[1].Length == 2 is false (:822-842); DomainMatches('evil.com.', 'com.', false) is true (:660-674), so the cookie is stored with Domain 'com.' (:459-461) and later matches any host ending in '.com.'. Same for 'co.uk.' (three labels). Checked on .NET 8: new Uri("http://evil.com./x").Host == "evil.com."; not run on Unity Mono, whose Uri comes from the same reference source. title: [Middleware] The built-in public-suffix heuristic misses longer and regional suffixes, so the default jar accepts cross-tenant Domain cookies
body:
## Summary
IsRejectedPublicSuffix rejects single labels, a small list of multi-label suffixes and 11 names under two-letter TLDs. Suffixes such as s3.amazonaws.com, blogspot.de or nsw.edu.au pass, so one tenant can set cookies for all tenants of a shared suffix unless the app configures an isPublicSuffix predicate.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:831`

## Problem
IsRejectedPublicSuffix (822-842) rejects single labels, an exact entry of KnownMultiLabelPublicSuffixes, and `<one of 11 names>.<2-letter TLD>`. Anything else passes: three-label or deeper suffixes (`s3.amazonaws.com`, `eu-west-1.elasticbeanstalk.com`, `nsw.edu.au`, `k12.ca.us`) and two-label suffixes outside the 11 names (`kiev.ua`, `blogspot.de`, `tokyo.jp`). The code comment says the list is a heuristic (38-39) and the constructor offers an isPublicSuffix hook (158), but the default CookieInterceptor constructs `new CookieJar()` without one (CookieInterceptor.cs:42).

**Failure scenario.** `tenant-a.blogspot.de` answers `Set-Cookie: session=X; Domain=blogspot.de`: the cookie is stored and sent to every other *.blogspot.de host (cookie tossing / session fixation between tenants).

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 section 5.3 step 5

## Suggested fix
Ship a compact Public Suffix List snapshot (or at least reject a Domain attribute when no predicate is configured and the domain has fewer labels than host minus one on known hosting TLD patterns), and document that production use needs the predicate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The default jar rejects Domain attributes that equal a public suffix using a bundled Public Suffix List snapshot, or documents and enforces that a predicate is required for production use

title: [Middleware] DecompressionInterceptor applies its own 32 MB decoded-size cap, unrelated to MaxBufferedResponseBodySize, including to streams
body:
## Summary
The decompression cap defaults to 32 MB while the client's buffered body limit defaults to 100 MB, and the cap also applies to streamed responses. Raising the client option does not raise the decode cap, and large streamed downloads fail mid-stream with a generic error. A compressed-limit field is aliased and a constructor flag is a no-op.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:39`

## Problem
DecompressionInterceptor.DefaultMaxDecompressedBodySizeBytes is 32 MB (DecompressionInterceptor.cs:20) while UHttpClientOptions.DefaultMaxBufferedResponseBodySize is 100 MB and is documented as not capping streaming responses (UHttpClientOptions.cs:109-121). DecompressionBodySource enforces the 32 MB cap on streamed bodies as well (DecompressionHandler.cs:309-326; asserted by DecompressionLimitAndAllocationTests.cs:30-40). `_maxCompressedBodySizeBytes` is a separate field that is always assigned the decoded limit (DecompressionHandler.cs:16, 38-39, 66), so the 'compressed' limit is not a real knob. The limit is fixed per interceptor instance; there is no per-request metadata key, unlike the redirect settings. `automaticDecompression: false` constructs an interceptor that does nothing (DecompressionInterceptor.cs:55-56).

**Failure scenario.** An app raises MaxBufferedResponseBodySize to 200 MB, or streams a 60 MB gzip-encoded catalogue to disk; both fail after 32 MB decoded with "Response decompression failed" (Unknown), mid-stream in the second case after 32 MB was already written, and nothing in the client options points to the DecompressionInterceptor constructor.

## Suggested fix
Derive the default from the client option (or expose the decode cap next to it) and state in UHttpClientOptions that a decoding interceptor applies its own cap to streams. Remove the aliased field and the flag argument, or make them real settings.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The default decode cap is derived from the client option, or the cap is exposed next to it, and UHttpClientOptions documents that a decoding interceptor caps streams
- [ ] The aliased _maxCompressedBodySizeBytes field and the no-op constructor flag are removed or made real settings
- [ ] Exceeding the cap yields a descriptive UHttpException naming the limit
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Middleware] DecompressionHandler counts only the outermost layer's output, so stacked codings burn CPU that cancellation cannot stop
body:
## Summary
DecompressionHandler checks the decoded-size limit against the output of the top stream only. Bytes passed between stacked inflate layers are never counted, and DEFLATE can consume large input for zero output, so the limit never trips. The buffered path is a synchronous loop without a CancellationToken, so neither the request timeout nor the caller's token interrupts it. A hostile server can pin a thread for minutes to hours with a small body.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:202`

## Problem
The limit is checked against `output.Length` of the top stream only (DecompressBufferedBody 200-223) and `_bytesRead` of the top stream (DecompressionBodySource.ReadAsync 309-326). Bytes passed between stacked InflateLayerStreams are never counted, and DEFLATE can consume any amount of input for zero output (empty stored blocks `00 00 00 FF FF`, empty gzip members), so the limit never trips. The buffered path is a synchronous loop without a CancellationToken (187-232); in the streaming path ct is only seen by the top-level ReadAsync, and lower layers read synchronously through BodySourceStream.Read with CancellationToken.None (548-564) wherever DeflateStream.ReadAsync falls back to Read. `_maxCompressedBodySizeBytes` (66) applies only to a known Content-Length. Measured in a scratch program with the same pull model (three stacked GZipStreams): 651 wire bytes -> 145 KB -> 100 MB -> 0 output bytes, 129 ms on a desktop core; each extra layer multiplies the work by roughly 700-1000.

**Failure scenario.** Response `Content-Encoding: gzip, gzip, gzip, gzip` with a ~1 KB body (four nested layers over empty stored blocks) needs ~100 GB of inflate work and yields no output: in the buffered path the handler thread spins for minutes to hours and neither the request timeout nor the caller's token stops it; in the streaming path one ReadAsync never returns. With a 32 MB compressed body (the allowed maximum) two layers already give ~30 GB of work.

## Suggested fix
Bound what every lower layer may produce (for example total intermediate bytes <= k x maxDecompressedBodySizeBytes, or a consumed-input budget per produced byte), count compressed input for unknown-length bodies, and add a cancellation/disposed checkpoint to the buffered loop and to InflateLayerStream's refill path. Keep it together with the chain cap of mw-protocol-01.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Intermediate output of every stacked inflate layer is bounded (for example total intermediate bytes <= k x maxDecompressedBodySizeBytes) and exceeding it fails with UHttpException
- [ ] Compressed input consumed for a body without known length is counted against a budget, so zero-output DEFLATE input cannot run unbounded
- [ ] The buffered decode loop and InflateLayerStream's refill path observe cancellation and disposal
- [ ] A response with several nested gzip layers over empty stored blocks fails fast with a bounded amount of work; A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-protocol-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: The limit only sees the outermost decoder's output: DecompressBufferedBody checks output.Length (DecompressionHandler.cs:202-223) and DecompressionBodySource checks _bytesRead (:309-326); bytes handed between stacked InflateLayerStreams are never counted, and _maxCompressedBodySizeBytes applies only to a known Content-Length (:66). The buffered loop takes no CancellationToken (:187-232); lower layers refill synchronously (InflateLayerStream.cs:628) and BodySourceStream.Read uses CancellationToken.None (DecompressionHandler.cs:559-563). The only reader is ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:180 (one ReadAsync at a time), so nothing aborts a read that produces no output; a lower layer does re-check disposal on entry (InflateLayerStream.cs:168/258), but nobody disposes while the single reader is stuck. Measured with a copy of InflateLayerStream.cs on .NET 8: a 909-byte body under three gzip layers expands to 218 KB, then 150 MB of empty stored blocks, yields 0 output bytes and takes 478 ms; each further layer multiplies the work by about 700, and the limit never trips. Distinct from mw-protocol-01: a chain cap of 3-5 does not bound this.

Related: #182, [[R11-mw-protocol-01]].

title: [Middleware] Each compressed response allocates about 16 KB of unpooled buffers plus a redundant BufferedStream copy per coding
body:
## Summary
DecompressionBodySource builds BodySourceStream, BufferedStream (8 KB) and InflateLayerStream (8 KB input array, unpooled) per coding, plus a DeflateStream per gzip member. Every compressed byte is copied through BufferedStream because the inflater requests sizes below its bypass threshold. Small gzip API responses therefore produce about 20 KB of garbage each, and the production transport never reaches the pooled copy-free buffered decode path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:269`

## Problem
DecompressionBodySource's constructor (DecompressionHandler.cs:268-270) builds BodySourceStream -> BufferedStream(8 KB) -> InflateLayerStream per coding. BufferedStream allocates its 8 KB array on first read and InflateLayerStream allocates `_in = new byte[InputBufferBytes]` (8 KB, InflateLayerStream.cs:76; deliberately unpooled, 41) per layer, then a DeflateStream per gzip member (on Mono plus a 4 KB managed io_buffer and native state). InflateLayerStream asks its source for `_in.Length - start` bytes with `start` up to HistoryBytes (PrepareInflaterFill, 612-616, 627-628), which is below BufferedStream's 8 KB bypass threshold after the first fill, so every compressed byte is copied inner -> BufferedStream buffer -> `_in` -> inflater. BufferedStream adds nothing: InflateLayerStream already buffers its input. Per response also: List<CompressionKind>(4) + ToArray + Substring per token (742-780) and a full header clone (77). Because RawSocketTransport only produces streaming sources (see mw-runtime-03), the SegmentedBuffer path of #74 (187-232) is not used for real traffic and buffered sends pay inflater -> rented 16 KB -> SegmentedBuffer.Write (ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:175-187).

**Failure scenario.** A game polls a JSON API that answers with 400-byte gzip bodies: each response costs roughly 20 KB of short-lived managed arrays (8 KB + 8 KB + 4 KB on Mono) and about ten objects for a 400-byte payload; at 20 responses per second that is 400 KB/s of garbage on Boehm/incremental GC from decompression alone.

## Suggested fix
Remove the BufferedStream layer (read the body source straight into `_in`); size `_in` from the known compressed Content-Length when it is small; parse Content-Encoding without the List/Substring for the single-token case. Consider decoding through the segment path when the wrapped source reports a small known length.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The BufferedStream layer is removed and the body source is read straight into the inflater's input buffer
- [ ] The input buffer is sized from a small known compressed Content-Length, and a single-token Content-Encoding is parsed without List/Substring allocations
- [ ] Managed allocation for a 400-byte gzip response is measured before and after and drops by at least the removed 8 KB BufferedStream array
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test (allocation gate under Tests/Runtime/Performance/ or Tests/Runtime/Middleware/) fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-runtime-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Facts hold. Per coding layer: BodySourceStream + BufferedStream(8 KB) + InflateLayerStream (DecompressionHandler.cs:268-270) with `_in = new byte[8192]` (InflateLayerStream.cs:76) and a DeflateStream per member (447). The first fill asks BufferedStream for 8192 bytes (bypass), every later fill asks for less (PrepareFill/PrepareInflaterFill keep the window, 567-574, 612-616), so BufferedStream allocates its 8 KB array and adds a copy while InflateLayerStream already buffers its own input. Content-Encoding parse allocates a List, an array and a Substring per token (742-780) and the headers are cloned (77). The pooled segment path (81-135, 187-232) is unreachable from RawSocketTransport because both body sources return false from TryGetBufferedData. The unpooled `_in` is a documented, sound trade-off (InflateLayerStream.cs:41: a dispose racing a read must not return a buffer in use); the BufferedStream layer and the unused buffered path have no such reason. #434 tracks per-read allocations of the streaming inflate path on Mono, not this fixed per-response cost. The 4 KB Mono io_buffer figure is from Mono's DeflateStreamNative and was not re-measured.

title: [Middleware] DecompressionBodySource.Abort disposes the DeflateStream while another thread may be inside its Read
body:
## Summary
Abort calls DisposeStreams before aborting the inner source, and InflateLayerStream.Dispose disposes the inflater while a reader thread may be inside Read or ReadAsync. On Unity 2021.3's Mono class library, DeflateStreamNative.Dispose frees a GCHandle that the native read callback resolves on every call. A concurrent dispose can therefore make the next callback resolve a freed or reused handle.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:378`

## Problem
DecompressionBodySource.Abort calls DisposeStreams before `_inner.Abort()` (DecompressionHandler.cs:372-380, 474-506); InflateLayerStream.Dispose swaps `_inflater` out and disposes it (InflateLayerStream.cs:750-766) while the reader thread may be inside `CurrentInflater().Read/ReadAsync` (178, 228). The class remarks (36-42) cover the layer's own fields but rely on DeflateStream tolerating a concurrent Dispose. In Unity 2021.3.45f2's System.dll DeflateStreamNative.Dispose calls SafeHandle.Dispose and GCHandle.Free, and the static UnmanagedRead callback does GCHandle.FromIntPtr(...).Target on every invocation from the native inflate loop. BufferedStream.Dispose likewise nulls its buffer under a reader.

**Failure scenario.** A consumer disposes a streaming response synchronously while a read is decoding (UHttpStreamingResponse.Dispose -> Abort when the body is not at end of stream). If the free lands between two feeder callbacks of one native read, the next callback resolves a freed handle: normally a null target and an IOException, but a handle slot reused by another DeflateStream created at that moment would make this read pull bytes from another response's compressed stream. Needs a Mono stress test (abort during active decode, many concurrent responses) to confirm.

## Suggested fix
Give the inflater one owner: on Abort mark the source aborted and abort the inner source (which ends the pending read), and let the reader dispose the decoder chain when it unwinds; dispose it from Abort only when no read is in flight.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The inflater has a single owner: Abort marks the source aborted and aborts the inner source, and the reading thread disposes the decoder chain when it unwinds
- [ ] The decoder chain is disposed from Abort only when no read is in flight
- [ ] Disposing a streaming response during an in-flight read ends the read with an exception and never touches a freed inflater
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ that disposes during a blocked read fails before the fix

title: [Middleware] DecompressionBodySource inflates the rest of the body for up to 2 s in DrainAsync/DisposeAsync instead of delegating
body:
## Summary
DrainAsync and DisposeAsync loop ReadAsync (inflate plus checksum) into a 16 KB buffer for up to 2 s whenever the body is not complete, with no byte budget, before calling the inner DisposeAsync. This replaces the transport's bounded drain on HTTP/1.1 and the immediate RST_STREAM on HTTP/2. Cancelling a large compressed download or discarding a compressed redirect or retry body keeps downloading and inflating for 2 s on mobile data.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:393`

## Problem
DrainAsync (DecompressionHandler.cs:351-370) loops ReadAsync (inflate + CRC32/Adler) into a 16 KB buffer; DisposeAsync (393-435) drains that way under a 2 s timer whenever `_completed` is 0, with no byte budget, and only then calls `_inner.DisposeAsync()`; GetTrailersAsync (387-388) does the same. The policies it overrides: Http11ResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync drains only keep-alive bodies whose remaining length fits `_bufferedDrainReuseThresholdBytes` and otherwise closes at once (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:279-316, 450-476); Http2ResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync resets the stream without draining (Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:276-279). architecture.md 'Body wrappers (decompression, ...) delegate DrainAsync, Abort, GetTrailersAsync'. DecompressionEarlyDisposeTests.cs:15-19,38 states that an early dispose never reaches the trailer; with this code the dispose drain does read to the trailer, fails the CRC, and the failure is swallowed at DecompressionHandler.cs:410-416 with the inner source aborted, so the test passes for a different reason.

**Failure scenario.** `await using` a streamed 200 MB gzip download and leave after the first kilobyte (user cancels): instead of closing the connection or sending RST_STREAM, the wrapper keeps downloading and inflating at full speed for 2 s (tens of MB of mobile data, one busy core), DisposeAsync takes 2 s, then the source is aborted anyway. A redirect or retry that discards a compressed 3xx/5xx body (RedirectHandler.DiscardBodyAsync -> ResponseBodyDiscardHelper.DrainAsync) inflates and checksums bytes nobody reads, and a corrupt or over-limit discarded body aborts a connection the transport could have reused.

## Suggested fix
In DrainAsync and DisposeAsync drop the decoder and delegate to `_inner.DrainAsync(ct)` / `_inner.DisposeAsync()` so the transport decides between drain and close; mark the wrapper completed. Keep decode-to-end only where validation is the point. Fix the test's stated reason.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] DrainAsync and DisposeAsync drop the decoder and delegate to the inner source's DrainAsync(ct) and DisposeAsync() so the transport chooses between drain and close
- [ ] The wrapper is marked completed after delegation and DisposeAsync no longer takes 2 s on an unfinished body
- [ ] Decode-to-end is kept only where validation is the purpose
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ shows the inner source is disposed immediately and no further bytes are read; the existing test's stated reason is corrected

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-runtime-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: resource-management.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described. DecompressionBodySource.DisposeAsync (DecompressionHandler.cs:393-435) drains through ReadAsync (inflate + checksum) under a 2 s timer with no byte budget whenever _completed is 0, then disposes the inner source; DrainAsync (351-370) and GetTrailersAsync (387-388) do the same. UHttpStreamingResponse.DisposeAsync always reaches it (UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:111-118, 228-238; only sync Dispose aborts an unfinished body, 155-160). The inner policies it replaces: Http11ResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync closes at once unless keep-alive and the remainder fits the 64 KB threshold (279-316, 450-476); Http2ResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync resets the stream (276-279). InflateLayerStream's own contract says 'disposing before the end skips the checks by design' (InflateLayerStream.cs:22-23) and architecture.md:102 asks wrappers to delegate. DecompressionEarlyDisposeTests.cs:27-41: the 256 KB mock body is drained by the dispose, the corrupt CRC is hit, ReadAsync throws, and DisposeAsync's bare catch (410-416) swallows it, so the test passes for a different reason than its doc comment states. The older phase-22a.5 review accepted the decoding DrainAsync only because the decoder stays in use; that does not hold in DisposeAsync, where the decoder is discarded.

Also reported as `mw-design-26` (merged into this issue).

title: [Middleware] Streaming decompression on Unity allocates a closure, task and state machine per read via Task.Run and DeflateStream.BeginRead
body:
## Summary
ReadFromDecompressionStreamAsync wraps each read in Task.Run when a SynchronizationContext is present, which costs a closure, delegate, Task and boxed state machine per read. On Unity the offload is redundant because Stream.ReadAsync already runs DeflateStream.Read on a pool thread through BeginRead/EndRead, which allocates again. A main-thread consumer reading a 10 MB gzip stream in 4 KB steps performs about 2,500 Task.Run round trips.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:469`

## Problem
ReadFromDecompressionStreamAsync wraps the read in `Task.Run(async () => await _decompressionStream.ReadAsync(destination, ct)..., ct)` whenever SynchronizationContext.Current is set (DecompressionHandler.cs:463-471): a closure, a delegate, a Task<int> and a boxed state machine per read for main-thread consumers. On Unity the offload is redundant, because Stream.ReadAsync already runs DeflateStream.Read on a pool thread through BeginRead/EndRead (class-library IL, see mw-runtime-02), which itself allocates a delegate, an async result and a task per read. The buffered decode uses `decompressionStream.Read(span)` (DecompressionHandler.cs:218); Unity's DeflateStream has no Span override, so Stream.Read(Span) rents an array and copies each 16 KB read. ProbePastLimitAsync allocates `new byte[1]` (439).

**Failure scenario.** The measured 4.3 KB/read of #434 and 1.7 KB/read of #416 for the decompression scenario include these frames; a main-thread consumer reading a 10 MB gzip stream in 4 KB steps performs about 2,500 Task.Run round trips.

## Suggested fix
Covered by the redesign in mw-runtime-03 (no pull through DeflateStream.ReadAsync). Until then drop the Task.Run on runtimes where ReadAsync is already offloaded and read into arrays, not spans, on the buffered path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The Task.Run offload is removed on runtimes where ReadAsync is already offloaded, and the buffered path reads into arrays rather than spans
- [ ] Allocations per streaming read for the decompression scenario are measured before and after and the gate budget in the streaming allocation tests is lowered accordingly
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test (Tests/Runtime/Performance/ gate) fails before the fix

title: [Middleware] Streamed gzip reads on Unity call BodySourceStream.Read with CancellationToken.None, losing cancellation and Abort
body:
## Summary
On Unity's Mono/IL2CPP class library DeflateStream only overrides the synchronous Read, so every ReadAsync falls back to a sync read of the base stream. BodySourceStream.Read bridges to the async body source with CancellationToken.None, so the caller's token and the 2 s dispose-drain bound are never observed, and Abort is a no-op once DisposeAsync has started. A stalled or half-open connection leaves ReadAsync and DisposeAsync hanging with a pool thread, buffer and connection held.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:559`

## Problem
DecompressionBodySource.ReadAsync -> ReadFromDecompressionStreamAsync (DecompressionHandler.cs:459-472) -> InflateLayerStream.ReadCoreAsync `await CurrentInflater().ReadAsync(buffer, cancellationToken)` (InflateLayerStream.cs:228). In Unity 2021.3.45f2's System.dll (unityjit and unityaot profiles, type metadata and IL read with System.Reflection.Metadata) DeflateStream overrides only Read(byte[],int,int), BeginRead (ReadMethod.BeginInvoke) and EndRead; mscorlib's Stream.ReadAsync(Memory) -> ReadAsync(byte[]) -> BeginEndReadAsync, and DeflateStreamNative.UnmanagedRead calls Stream.Read on the base stream. So the inflater pulls input synchronously: InflaterInput.Read -> ReadForInflater `_source.Read(_in, ...)` (InflateLayerStream.cs:618-628) -> BufferedStream -> BodySourceStream.Read (DecompressionHandler.cs:548-564), which blocks on `_inner.ReadAsync(..., CancellationToken.None).GetAwaiter().GetResult()`. For streaming sends the transport adds no token of its own (RawSocketTransport.cs:1826-1830; Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:26-28 'body reads are governed only by the consumer token'). DisposeAsync (393-435) sets `_disposeStarted`, then drains through the same ReadAsync with a 2 s token (404-405) that is only checked between reads; Abort (372-380) returns immediately when `_disposeStarted` is set, and UHttpStreamingResponse.AbortBody (UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:142-148) is a no-op after dispose. The baseline rationale for the two GetResult sites (Tools~/ci/analyzer-baseline.txt:34-37, 'the library itself reads asynchronously') does not hold on these runtimes. No test reads or disposes a stalled compressed body with a cancellable token (rg 'Cancel' Tests/Runtime/Middleware/Decompression*.cs: only CancellationToken.None).

**Failure scenario.** Unity player or Editor, SendStreamingAsync of a gzip response; the server stalls mid-body or the mobile network drops and leaves a half-open socket. `await body.ReadAsync(buffer, cts.Token)` does not return when cts is cancelled. `await response.DisposeAsync()` never completes: the drain read is blocked, its 2 s token is never observed, and a pool thread, the 16 KB drain buffer, the connection and its per-host slot stay held. A later Abort cannot release them because it is ignored once dispose started. (Buffered sends are bounded by the transport read token.)

## Suggested fix
Feed the inflater only from `_in` that InflateLayerStream fills asynchronously with the caller's token (so the bridge never blocks; treat a starved inflater read as 'need input', see mw-runtime-03), or at least pass the token of the read in progress to BodySourceStream.Read. Make Abort always abort the inner source, also while DisposeAsync drains. Add a PlayMode test with a held compressed source: cancel a read, then DisposeAsync.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The inflater is fed only from an input buffer that InflateLayerStream fills asynchronously with the caller's token, or the token of the read in progress reaches BodySourceStream.Read
- [ ] Cancelling the token ends a pending streamed read with OperationCanceledException and DisposeAsync completes within its bound on a stalled source
- [ ] Abort always aborts the inner source, also while DisposeAsync is draining
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test with a held compressed source fails before the fix; a PlayMode test on Unity's class library is run and recorded

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-runtime-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Re-traced, including the class-library part. Unity 2021.3.45f2 unityaot-linux System.dll (read with System.Reflection.Metadata): DeflateStream declares only Read(byte[],int,int), BeginRead, EndRead (no ReadAsync / Read(Span) override); BeginRead IL = newobj ReadMethod + callvirt ReadMethod::BeginInvoke; DeflateStreamNative.UnmanagedRead IL calls Stream::Read on the base stream; mscorlib Stream.ReadAsync(Memory) -> ReadAsync(byte[]) (token checked once) -> BeginEndReadAsync. So InflateLayerStream.cs:228 runs the inflater's synchronous read on a pool thread, which pulls through InflaterInput.Read (792-800) -> ReadForInflater `_source.Read` (618-628) -> BufferedStream -> BodySourceStream.Read, blocking in `_inner.ReadAsync(..., CancellationToken.None).GetAwaiter().GetResult()` (DecompressionHandler.cs:559-563). Streaming sends give the inner source no transport token (RawSocketTransport.cs:1826-1830, Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:26-28) and ResponseBodyStream registers nothing on the caller token (ResponseBodyStream.cs:145-160), so a body-phase read on a stalled HTTP/1.1 connection ignores cancellation. UHttpStreamingResponse.DisposeAsync always calls _bodySource.DisposeAsync (UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:111-118, 228-238); DecompressionBodySource.DisposeAsync sets _disposeStarted (395) and drains through the same read with a 2 s token that is only checked between reads (404-405, 299); Abort returns at 374-375 and AbortBody at UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:144-145, so nothing can release it. No refuting guard or test (Tests/Runtime/Middleware/Decompression*.cs use only CancellationToken.None, no held source). Limits of the claim: header/trailer phases read asynchronously with the token (InflateLayerStream.cs:246); sync Dispose()/Body.Dispose() before DisposeAsync still abort (UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:155-160); HTTP/2 has its own stall timeout; buffered sends are bounded by the transport token. Not run on a device, but the path is fixed by the shipped IL.

title: [Middleware] Over-limit and corrupt compressed bodies map to UHttpErrorType.Unknown while Core uses NetworkError for the same cap
body:
## Summary
CreateDecompressionError maps every decode failure, including both size limits, to Unknown with a fixed message. Core maps an over-limit buffered body to NetworkError, which is retryable, while Unknown is not. A 150 MB identity response is retried by RetryInterceptor but the same body gzip-encoded fails at 32 MB as Unknown and is not. Callers can only tell too-large, corrupt and redirect-policy failures apart by matching message text.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:721`

## Problem
CreateDecompressionError maps every decode failure, including both size limits, to UHttpErrorType.Unknown with the fixed message "Response decompression failed." (DecompressionHandler.cs:66-74, 451-457, 721-725). Core's collector maps the same condition, a body over MaxBufferedResponseBodySize, to NetworkError (ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:274-282, documented in UHttpClientOptions.cs:116). NetworkError is retryable and Unknown is not (UHttpError.cs:68-91). RedirectHandler reports redirect limit, loop and blocked downgrade as InvalidRequest, documented as "Invalid request configuration" (RedirectHandler.cs:173, 185, 197; UHttpError.cs:26), and a non-replayable body on 307/308 as InvalidRequest too (RedirectInterceptor.cs:229). RedirectHandler's constructor calls initialRequest.Uri.AbsoluteUri (RedirectHandler.cs:73), which throws InvalidOperationException for a relative Uri, so that case surfaces as Unknown with the redirect interceptor and as InvalidRequest from the transport without it (RawSocketTransport.cs:444-449).

**Failure scenario.** A 150 MB identity response fails as NetworkError and RetryInterceptor downloads it again; the same body with Content-Encoding: gzip fails at 32 MB as Unknown and is not retried. An app cannot tell "too large", "corrupt", "redirect loop" and "unexpected exception" apart except by matching message text.

## Suggested fix
Decide the type for each class once (response over a configured cap; malformed response content; redirect policy refusal) and use it in Core, decompression and redirect; if the enum cannot grow before GA, at least use the same existing value for the same condition and expose a stable discriminator instead of message text.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One UHttpErrorType is decided per class (response over a configured cap, malformed response content, redirect policy refusal) and used consistently in Core, DecompressionHandler and RedirectHandler
- [ ] Callers can distinguish the classes through a stable discriminator rather than message text
- [ ] The error type table is documented in UHttpError and the retry behaviour follows from it
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ asserts the error type for each class and fails before the change

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-design-08` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Facts hold: every decode failure including both size limits is UHttpErrorType.Unknown with a fixed message (DecompressionHandler.cs:66-74, 451-457, 721-725); Core maps an over-limit buffered body to NetworkError (ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:274-282, documented at UHttpClientOptions.cs:114-116), which IsRetryable treats as retryable while Unknown is not (UHttpError.cs:69-91); redirect limit, loop, blocked downgrade and non-replayable body are InvalidRequest (RedirectHandler.cs:173, 185, 197; RedirectInterceptor.cs:229). Transport-level truncation still surfaces as the inner source's own UHttpException, passed through unchanged (DecompressionHandler.cs:334-338), so only genuinely corrupt or over-limit compressed content is Unknown. This is an inconsistent error taxonomy with no single wrong outcome beyond the retry difference; worth deciding before GA, but low. The relative-Uri sub-claim (RedirectHandler.cs:73) was not pursued: client-created requests are always absolute.

Related: [[R11-mw-protocol-30]].

title: [Middleware] Corrupt or truncated gzip/deflate bodies are reported as UHttpErrorType.Unknown instead of NetworkError
body:
## Summary
CreateDecompressionError reports truncation, corruption and the size limit alike as Unknown with the message "Response decompression failed.". The transport reports malformed or truncated responses as NetworkError, which is retryable, while Unknown is documented as an unexpected exception. A gzip body cut by a dropped connection on an idempotent GET is therefore not retried, unlike the same fault on an identity body.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:724`

## Problem
CreateDecompressionError builds UHttpError(UHttpErrorType.Unknown, "Response decompression failed.") for corrupt data, truncation and the size limit alike (721-725). The transport maps malformed responses to NetworkError (RawSocketTransport.cs:810-818) and UHttpError.IsRetryable treats NetworkError as retryable and Unknown as not (Core/UHttpError.cs:68-90); Unknown is documented as 'unexpected exception'.

**Failure scenario.** A gzip body cut by a dropped connection on an idempotent GET: the same network fault that would be retried for an identity body is surfaced as a non-retryable Unknown error, and callers cannot tell a limit violation from a transient truncation.

## Suggested fix
Report truncated or corrupt coded bodies as NetworkError (malformed response) and keep a distinct, non-retryable error for the size limit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Truncated or corrupt coded bodies are reported as NetworkError (malformed response)
- [ ] The size-limit violation keeps a distinct, non-retryable error
- [ ] IsRetryable behaves as for identity bodies on a truncated gzip GET
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ truncates a gzip body and asserts the error type; it fails before the fix

title: [Middleware] DecompressionHandler honours only the first Content-Encoding field line but removes all of them
body:
## Summary
TryResolveCompression reads headers.Get("Content-Encoding"), which returns the first value only, while forwardHeaders.Remove drops every line. RFC 9110 section 5.3 treats several field lines as one comma-separated list. With two gzip lines one layer is decoded and the caller receives gzip bytes labelled as plain content; with gzip then br the handler decodes in the wrong order and fails with an invalid GZIP header.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:735`

## Problem
TryResolveCompression reads `headers.Get("Content-Encoding")` (735); HttpHeaders.Get returns the first value only (Core/HttpHeaders.cs:70-75) and the parsers add one value per field line (Http11ResponseParser.cs:301-302, HpackDecoder.cs:196/261). `forwardHeaders.Remove("Content-Encoding")` (78) then drops all lines. RFC 9110 section 5.3 makes several lines equal to one comma-separated list. DecompressionInterceptorTests.MultiValueContentEncoding_IsDecompressedInReverseOrder covers only one comma-joined line.

**Failure scenario.** `Content-Encoding: gzip` followed by a second line `Content-Encoding: gzip` (double compressed): one layer is decoded, both header lines are removed, and the caller receives gzip bytes labelled as plain content. `Content-Encoding: gzip` + `Content-Encoding: br`: the handler decodes gzip first although br is the outer coding and fails with `The GZIP header is invalid` instead of passing the response through. It is also how a chain cap would be bypassed (curl CVE-2023-23916).

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 sections 5.3, 8.4

## Suggested fix
Build the chain from GetValues("Content-Encoding") in field-line order and apply the pass-through rule (any unknown coding -> untouched) to the combined list.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The coding chain is built from GetValues("Content-Encoding") in field-line order
- [ ] The pass-through rule (any unknown coding leaves the response untouched) applies to the combined list
- [ ] Repeated gzip lines decode all layers, and gzip plus br passes the response through undecoded
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ with multiple Content-Encoding field lines fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-protocol-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: TryResolveCompression reads headers.Get("Content-Encoding") (DecompressionHandler.cs:735); HttpHeaders.Get returns values[0] only (Core/HttpHeaders.cs:70-75) and the parser adds one value per field line (Http11ResponseParser.cs:301-302). forwardHeaders.Remove("Content-Encoding") (:78) drops all lines (HttpHeaders.cs:98-102). Two lines 'gzip' + 'gzip' therefore decode one layer and forward gzip bytes with no Content-Encoding; 'gzip' + 'br' decodes gzip against br bytes and fails instead of passing through. Tests only use a single Set("Content-Encoding", ...) line (DecompressionInterceptorTests.cs:232). Split Content-Encoding lines are uncommon in practice.

Related: [[R11-mw-protocol-01]].

title: [Middleware] DecompressionHandler accepts an unbounded number of content codings, forcing thousands of stacked inflaters
body:
## Summary
TryResolveCompression appends every gzip/deflate token to the chain with no cap and builds one InflateLayerStream per token, each with an 8 KB input array. The only bound is the header size, about 1,630 codings on HTTP/1.1 and about 51,000 on HTTP/2. A hostile server can force hundreds of MB of allocation before any body byte is read, or deep recursion on the first read that can overflow the stack.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:742`

## Problem
TryResolveCompression (DecompressionHandler.cs:727-782) appends every gzip/x-gzip/deflate token to `resolved` with no cap, and CreateDecompressionStream (684-700) builds one InflateLayerStream per token. Each InflateLayerStream allocates an 8 KB input array in its field initializer (InflateLayerStream.cs:76) and a DeflateStream at StartBody (445-447); every read recurses through all layers (InflateLayerStream.Read 166-197 -> DeflateStream.Read -> InflaterInput.Read 792-800 -> ReadForInflater 618-639 -> _source.Read of the layer below). The only bound is the header size: 8192 chars per HTTP/1.1 line (Http11ResponseParser.cs:156), about 1630 codings; 256 KB of decoded header list on HTTP/2 (UHttpClientOptions.cs:14), about 51,000 codings. No test covers a chain limit (Tests/Runtime/Middleware has only 2-layer cases).

**Failure scenario.** A hostile or compromised server (or an on-path attacker on http) answers over HTTP/2 with `content-encoding: gzip,gzip,...` repeated ~51k times: the handler allocates ~420 MB of 8 KB arrays before reading one body byte (OOM on mobile). With ~1600 nested gzip layers over HTTP/1.1 (body about 40 KB) the first read recurses ~1600 x several managed/native frames; a stack overflow is not catchable and kills the player. Same class as curl CVE-2022-32206.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 section 8.4

## Suggested fix
Cap the chain (curl allows 5; 2-3 covers real servers) and fail with a UHttpException beyond the cap, counting codings across all Content-Encoding field lines (see mw-protocol-09). Add a regression test with a long chain.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The coding chain is capped (for example 3) counted across all Content-Encoding field lines
- [ ] A response over the cap fails with UHttpException before any inflater is allocated
- [ ] The cap is documented
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ with a long chain over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 header shapes fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-protocol-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: No cap exists: TryResolveCompression (Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:742-782) appends every gzip/x-gzip/deflate token and CreateDecompressionStream (:691-699) builds one InflateLayerStream per token, each with an 8 KB array in a field initializer (InflateLayerStream.cs:76); layers read each other recursively (Read :166-197, ReadForInflater :618-639). No test or guard limits the chain. Correction to the numbers: the default HTTP/2 bound is MaxHeaderListSize = 64 KB (Core/Http2Options.cs:15, enforced at Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:617), not 256 KB (UHttpClientOptions.cs:14 is only the ceiling when the user raises the setting), so the default is about 13,000 codings / ~105 MB, not 51k / 420 MB. HTTP/1.1: 8192-char line (Http11ResponseParser.cs:156) = ~1630 codings / 13 MB. Measured with a copy of InflateLayerStream.cs in a scratch .NET 8 program: 13,000 gzip layers over a 12-byte garbage body allocate 103 MB and die with an uncatchable stack overflow on a 1 MB thread stack (6,000 layers also overflow); 1,630 valid nested layers (38.5 KB body) survive a 1 MB stack but overflow a 512 KB stack. Not run on Unity Mono/IL2CPP. DecompressionInterceptor is opt-in, so not a default-path crash.

Related: [[R11-mw-protocol-02]], [[R11-mw-protocol-09]].

title: [Middleware] DecompressionInterceptor adds Accept-Encoding to Range requests and the handler tries to inflate 206 partial bodies
body:
## Summary
InvokeAsync adds Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate whenever the header is absent, including requests with Range or If-Range. A 206 response with Content-Encoding carries a byte range of the coded representation, which cannot be decoded alone, yet the handler decodes it and removes Content-Length while keeping Content-Range. A caller's Range request against precompressed assets fails with an invalid GZIP header or a truncation error.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionInterceptor.cs:68`

## Problem
InvokeAsync adds `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate` whenever the header is absent (DecompressionInterceptor.cs:68-73), also when the request carries Range/If-Range. HasNoContent exempts only 1xx/204/304/HEAD/empty bodies (DecompressionHandler.cs:164-179), so a 206 with Content-Encoding is decoded and its Content-Length removed (77-79) while Content-Range stays. A range of a gzip representation cannot be decoded on its own. FileDownloader works around it by forcing `Accept-Encoding: identity` (Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:386-390), which confirms the hazard; a caller's own Range request has no such guard. No test covers 206.

**Failure scenario.** `client.Get(url).WithHeader("Range", "bytes=1000-")` against a server with precompressed assets (nginx gzip_static, CDNs): the server answers 206 with `Content-Encoding: gzip` and bytes 1000.. of the .gz file; the handler fails the request with `Response decompression failed` (invalid GZIP header). With `bytes=0-99` it fails as truncated.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 sections 8.4, 14.2, 15.3.7

## Suggested fix
Do not add Accept-Encoding when the request has a Range header (or send identity), and pass 206 responses through undecoded with their headers intact.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Accept-Encoding is not added to requests carrying Range or If-Range
- [ ] 206 responses are passed through undecoded with their headers intact
- [ ] A caller's explicit Accept-Encoding is unchanged
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ for a Range request answered with a 206 gzip range fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-protocol-12` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: InvokeAsync adds 'Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate' whenever the header is absent, with no Range/If-Range check (DecompressionInterceptor.cs:68-73). HasNoContent exempts only 1xx/204/304/HEAD/empty bodies (DecompressionHandler.cs:164-179), so a 206 with Content-Encoding is inflated and its Content-Length removed (:77-79). A byte range of a coded representation cannot be decoded alone, so the request fails with 'Response decompression failed'. FileDownloader guards its own resume requests with 'Accept-Encoding: identity' (Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:386-390); a caller's own Range request has no such guard, and no test covers 206.

title: [Middleware] First-party interceptors each copy the request (up to four per send) and CopyWithSharedContent clones headers and metadata twice
body:
## Summary
DefaultHeadersInterceptor, DecompressionInterceptor, CookieInterceptor and AuthInterceptor each call request.CopyWithSharedContent() when they add a header. Each copy deep-clones the headers and metadata twice, so one send can perform four copies and eight clones. This adds allocations to every request through the default pipeline.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionInterceptor.cs:70`

## Problem
DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:46, DecompressionInterceptor.cs:70, CookieInterceptor.cs:67 and AuthInterceptor.cs:73 each call request.CopyWithSharedContent() when they add a header. CopyWithSharedContent (UHttpRequest.cs:514-525) passes `_headers.Clone()` and `new Dictionary<string, object>(_metadata)` to the private constructor, which clones both again (UHttpRequest.cs:144, 148-150; reported for Core as core-runtime-05). HttpHeaders.Clone allocates a dictionary plus one List<string> per header (HttpHeaders.cs:127-135). A copy made by an outer interceptor is already private to the dispatch, yet the next interceptor copies it again. Each interceptor also adds an async state machine and a handler object (DecompressionHandler, CookieHandler, RedirectHandler).

**Failure scenario.** Canonical pipeline with default headers, cookies, auth and decompression, request with 8 headers: 4 copies = 8 header clones (about 70 small objects) and 8 metadata dictionaries, roughly 8-10 KB of garbage per request before the transport runs, repeated for every redirect hop and retry attempt.

## Suggested fix
Fix the double clone in Core, and let interceptors reuse a dispatch-owned copy: mark copies made by CopyWithSharedContent (internal flag) and mutate such a request in place instead of copying it again (the header writes are idempotent Set calls), so a send makes at most one copy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CopyWithSharedContent clones headers and metadata once per call
- [ ] An interceptor that receives a request already copied by the dispatch chain mutates it in place instead of copying again
- [ ] A request passing through all four first-party interceptors allocates at most one request copy, measured in a test
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ counting request copies per send; it fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-runtime-08` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced: DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:46, DecompressionInterceptor.cs:70, CookieInterceptor.cs:67 and AuthInterceptor.cs:73 each call CopyWithSharedContent when they add a header, and CopyWithSharedContent clones headers and metadata (UHttpRequest.cs:518-524) before the private constructor clones both again (144, 147-149). The double clone is the Core finding core-runtime-05 (already confirmed in the Core batch) and is the larger half of the cost. The one-copy-per-interceptor part is the documented copy-on-write rule (architecture.md:98-101) and each copy happens only when that interceptor really adds a header; the cost is a few KB of garbage per request, not per read or frame. Real but minor once core-runtime-05 is fixed.

Related: #76, #120, [[R11-mw-design-10]].

title: [Middleware] DefaultHeadersInterceptor keeps the caller's HttpHeaders instance and enumerates it on dispatch threads without a snapshot or lock
body:
## Summary
The constructor stores the caller's HttpHeaders reference, and every dispatch enumerates its live Dictionary key collection. If the caller mutates the headers while requests are in flight, enumeration can throw InvalidOperationException or return torn values. HttpHeaders is not thread-safe, so the interceptor has no owner for this shared mutable field.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:20`

## Problem
The constructor stores the reference (`_defaultHeaders = defaultHeaders ?? new HttpHeaders()`, DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:20). Every dispatch enumerates `_defaultHeaders.Names`, the live Dictionary key collection (HttpHeaders.cs:108), and calls GetValues (DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:35-52). HttpHeaders is a Dictionary<string, List<string>> and is documented as not thread-safe (architecture.md:130). Core's own default headers are cloned at client construction (UHttpClientOptions.cs:186) and applied at CreateRequest (UHttpClient.cs:182), so the only reason to use this interceptor with overrideExisting=false is to change the headers after the client exists. architecture.md:112-114 requires cloning caller-owned configuration. The header copy loop is also a third copy of UHttpRequest.CopyHeaders (UHttpRequest.cs:585-600).

**Failure scenario.** After login the app calls defaults.Set("X-Session", id) on the main thread while requests are dispatching on pool threads: the foreach throws InvalidOperationException (collection modified), surfaced as UHttpException(Unknown), or a reader sees a List<string> mid-update.

## Suggested fix
Either snapshot the headers in the constructor (and document the interceptor as immutable) or provide a thread-safe update method that swaps an immutable snapshot with Volatile.Write. Reuse one header-copy helper from Core.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The interceptor snapshots the default headers at construction, or exposes a thread-safe update that swaps an immutable snapshot via Volatile.Write
- [ ] Mutating the caller's original HttpHeaders after construction does not affect or break in-flight dispatches
- [ ] The behaviour is documented in XML docs on the constructor
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ that mutates the source headers concurrently with dispatch; it fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-design-10` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: the constructor keeps the caller's instance (Runtime/Middleware/DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:20) and each dispatch enumerates the live Dictionary key collection (HttpHeaders.cs:108 `Names => _headers.Keys`) and reads the live List from GetValues (HttpHeaders.cs:82-87) at DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:33-52, with no lock or snapshot; HttpHeaders has no synchronisation (architecture.md:130). A concurrent Set/Add/Remove by the app would throw InvalidOperationException in the foreach, which UHttpClient wraps as UHttpException(Unknown) (UHttpClient.cs:429-434); the throw is also outside the try at lines 57-70, so an already-created requestForNext is not disposed and context.UpdateRequest is not rolled back. No guard found, no doc says the instance is snapshotted or must not be mutated, and the four tests in Tests/Runtime/Middleware/DefaultHeadersInterceptorTests.cs never mutate after construction. Downgraded to low: the trigger needs the app to mutate the passed HttpHeaders after construction while requests run past the first await on pool threads, which nothing documents as supported; the reviewer's claim that this is 'the only reason' to use the interceptor is speculation, and architecture.md:112 forbids mutating caller config, which this code does not do (it only reads). The duplicated copy loop (UHttpRequest.cs:585-600) is real but cosmetic.

Also reported as `mw-runtime-15` (merged into this issue).

title: [Middleware] DefaultHeadersInterceptor inside RedirectInterceptor re-adds Authorization, Cookie and API-key headers on cross-origin redirect hops
body:
## Summary
RedirectInterceptor strips Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie on a cross-origin hop and redispatches through the rest of the chain. If DefaultHeadersInterceptor is placed inside the redirect interceptor, it runs again for the new hop and adds the configured credential headers back. The credentials are then sent to a different origin, which breaks the rule that credentials stay with their origin.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:37`

## Problem
RedirectInterceptor.BuildRedirectRequest strips Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie on a cross-origin hop (RedirectInterceptor.cs:133-138) from its own copy of the request and redispatches through `next` (RedirectHandler.cs:242). DefaultHeadersInterceptor.Wrap (29-53) then runs again for the hop and adds every default header the hop request lacks (line 37; with overrideExisting it replaces unconditionally) with no origin check. AuthInterceptor received origin binding for exactly this pattern (#56, AuthInterceptor.cs:112-128); InterceptorOrdering has no rule for it (Core/Pipeline/InterceptorOrdering.cs:53-70) and the documentation lists RedirectInterceptor first (Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:12), so an interceptor added later is inside it. DefaultHeadersInterceptorTests has no redirect case.

**Failure scenario.** Interceptors = [RedirectInterceptor, DefaultHeadersInterceptor({Authorization: 'Bearer T'})]. api.example.com answers `302 Location: https://cdn.other.net/x`; the hop request reaches cdn.other.net carrying `Authorization: Bearer T`. With the order reversed the header is stripped, so the interceptor order decides whether the credential leaks.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 section 15.4

## Suggested fix
Bind credential default headers (at least Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie) to the origin of the first request seen on the RequestContext, as AuthInterceptor does, or let RedirectInterceptor mark cross-origin derived hops in the context and skip those headers there. Add both-order regression tests like AuthRedirectOrderTests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Credential default headers (at least Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie) are applied only for the origin of the first request seen on the RequestContext
- [ ] A cross-origin redirect hop carries none of the default credential headers, whatever the interceptor order
- [ ] Same-origin redirect hops keep the default headers
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ with DefaultHeadersInterceptor ordered inside RedirectInterceptor and a cross-origin 302; it fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-protocol-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: RedirectInterceptor.BuildRedirectRequest strips Authorization/Proxy-Authorization/Cookie on a cross-origin hop (RedirectInterceptor.cs:133-138) and RedirectHandler redispatches through the inner chain (RedirectHandler.cs:242). DefaultHeadersInterceptor.Wrap runs again for that hop and sets every default header the request lacks, with no origin check (DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:33-51), so a stripped Authorization or Cookie default comes back. No guard: InterceptorOrdering has only the Cache/Auth and Concurrency/Retry rules (Core/Pipeline/InterceptorOrdering.cs:53-70), DefaultHeadersInterceptor has no IInterceptorRole, Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:207 only says it 'adds headers to every request', and DefaultHeadersInterceptorTests has no redirect case. Needs the user to put a credential header into DefaultHeadersInterceptor and list it after RedirectInterceptor; that order is the documented default position for RedirectInterceptor. Custom headers such as X-Api-Key are not stripped by the redirect interceptor in either order, so the order dependence concerns Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie only.

Also reported as `mw-design-01` (merged into this issue).

Related: #117, [[R11-mw-design-10]].

title: [Middleware] Decompressed responses read through DeflateStream's async-over-sync path park a pool thread in GetResult() per pending network read
body:
## Summary
RawSocketTransport hands the handler streaming body sources, so DecompressionHandler decodes every compressed response through DeflateStream with a feeder that pulls from the network synchronously. On Unity this costs one thread-pool dispatch per read and one pool thread blocked in GetResult() while the network read is pending. This is sync-over-async on the response path and can starve a clamped thread pool.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/InflateLayerStream.cs:228`

## Problem
RawSocketTransport always hands the handler a streaming Http11ResponseBodySource/Http2ResponseBodySource (DispatchOnLeaseAsync -> EmitParsedResponseHeadAsync, RawSocketTransport.cs:1765-1843, 1862-1900; both sources return false from TryGetBufferedData), so DecompressionHandler takes the DecompressionBodySource path (DecompressionHandler.cs:137-140) for buffered sends as well; the segment-based buffered decode (81-135) is reached only by mock/replay transports. ResponseCollectorHandler.CollectAsync reads it in 16 KB steps (ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:175-187). On Unity each such read is Stream.ReadAsync -> DeflateStream.BeginRead -> delegate BeginInvoke on a pool thread -> native inflate -> UnmanagedRead -> Stream.Read -> InflateLayerStream.ReadForInflater (InflateLayerStream.cs:618-628) -> BodySourceStream.Read -> `GetAwaiter().GetResult()` (DecompressionHandler.cs:559-563), as traced in mw-runtime-02 against Unity 2021.3.45f2's System.dll/mscorlib. InflateLayerStream.ReadForInflaterAsync/RefillForInflaterAsync (641-669) never run there. Callers with a SynchronizationContext add a Task.Run hop on top (DecompressionHandler.cs:469-471). CLAUDE.md section 4 bans sync-over-async; the baseline entry accepts these two sites only as a bridge 'for sync callers' (analyzer-baseline.txt:34-37).

**Failure scenario.** A 4-core phone starts 8 parallel API calls whose responses are gzip (Accept-Encoding is injected by default). Each download parks one pool worker for most of its duration while the socket completions and CancelAfter timer callbacks that would unblock them are queued to the same pool; Mono only adds workers slowly when it detects starvation, so the batch stalls for hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, and with a capped pool (ThreadPool.SetMaxThreads) it does not recover. Even without starvation each 16 KB of decoded data costs a pool dispatch. The parked thread and the per-read dispatch are traced; the size of the stall needs a device run (N concurrent throttled gzip downloads with N >= processor count, measure completion latency and ThreadPool.GetAvailableThreads).

## Suggested fix
Stop letting the inflater pull from the network: in ReadCoreAsync await `_source.ReadAsync` into `_in` whenever it is empty, and make InflaterInput return 0 when `_in` is empty and the source has not ended, treating that inflater result as 'need input' instead of end of member (Mono's zlib helper leaves the stream usable after a starved read; verify on Mono and IL2CPP). Then no read blocks and the token is honoured. Keep the sync bridge only for explicit sync callers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The inflater never blocks on the network: ReadCoreAsync awaits the source into the input buffer whenever it is empty, and the feeder returns 0 when no input is buffered
- [ ] No GetResult()/Wait()/Result call remains on the decompression read path
- [ ] Decoded bytes are delivered as input arrives, not only once the destination buffer is full
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ with a source that delays input and asserts no thread is blocked while the read is pending; it fails before the fix
- [ ] Verified on Unity Mono and IL2CPP player builds and recorded

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-runtime-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Mechanism confirmed, impact size not measured. Both transport sources return false from TryGetBufferedData (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:93-97, Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:83-88), so DecompressionHandler.cs:81 is skipped and every real compressed response uses DecompressionBodySource (137-140), buffered sends included. On Unity each body-phase read is DeflateStream.BeginRead -> ReadMethod.BeginInvoke (IL of Unity 2021.3.45f2 System.dll checked, see mw-runtime-02), i.e. one pool dispatch per read, and each inflater refill blocks that pool thread in BodySourceStream.Read GetResult (DecompressionHandler.cs:559-563) while the socket read is pending; ReadForInflaterAsync/RefillForInflaterAsync (InflateLayerStream.cs:641-669) are unreachable there. The baseline rationale (Tools~/ci/analyzer-baseline.txt:34-35, 'the library itself reads asynchronously') is therefore wrong for Unity, and CLAUDE.md section 4 bans sync-over-async. Qualifier: the first fill is asynchronous (InflateLayerStream.cs:242-247), so a body whose compressed bytes arrive in that first read (up to 8 KB) never parks a thread, it only pays the dispatch. The thread-pool starvation in the scenario depends on Mono/IL2CPP pool injection and was not measured, so severity is medium rather than high; #434 tracks only the per-read allocation of this path, #447 a different pool stall.

Also reported as `mw-design-07` (merged into this issue).

Related: #182, #434, [[R11-mw-runtime-04]], [[R11-mw-protocol-11]], [[R11-mw-protocol-29]], [[R11-mw-runtime-20]].

title: [Middleware] Zero-length gzip body of unknown length fails as truncated and bytes after the gzip trailer fail validation
body:
## Summary
For a streaming body of unknown length, a gzip response with zero bytes reaches the header parser, which throws 'GZIP payload is truncated'. Any byte after the gzip trailer also fails validation. Browsers and curl accept both cases, so valid-in-practice servers produce failed requests.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/InflateLayerStream.cs:419`

## Problem
HasNoContent passes an empty body through only when its length is known or it is buffered (DecompressionHandler.cs:175-178). For a streaming body of unknown length the first read reaches TryReadGzipHeader -> NeedHeaderBytes, which throws `GZIP payload is truncated` when the source ended with zero bytes (InflateLayerStream.cs:417-423). After the trailer only end of input or another member is accepted (495-516); DecompressionZlibAndMultiMemberTests.Gzip_WithTrailingGarbage_Fails asserts it. Chromium's GzipSourceStream ignores bytes after the footer and treats an empty stream as empty content.

**Failure scenario.** A server answers `200`, `Content-Encoding: gzip`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and an empty body (seen from filters that set the header before knowing there is no content), or pads the gzip stream with NUL bytes: the request fails with `Response decompression failed` where a browser shows an empty or complete body.

## Spec reference
RFC 1952 section 2.2

## Suggested fix
Treat end of input before the first header byte as an empty body, and consider ignoring a bounded amount of trailing bytes for the outermost layer (as the raw-DEFLATE path already does with MaxBytesAfterRawEnd).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] End of input before the first gzip header byte is treated as an empty body
- [ ] A bounded amount of trailing bytes after the outermost gzip trailer is ignored, as the raw-DEFLATE path already does
- [ ] Truncation after at least one header byte, and corrupt trailers, still raise UHttpException
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ for the empty streaming body and the trailing bytes cases; it fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-protocol-29` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.
