title: [Middleware] Truncated raw-DEFLATE body (Content-Encoding: deflate without zlib wrapper) ends as a clean validated end of stream
body:
## Summary
For raw DEFLATE the decoder finishes as soon as the source ends, without checking whether the inflater reached its final block. The inflater-starved signal is only consulted for the zlib and gzip messages. A connection cut mid-body therefore yields a silently shortened response instead of an error.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/InflateLayerStream.cs:543`

## Problem
For Format.RawDeflate EndBody goes to Phase.RawDrain (457-466) and TryDrainRaw (543-555) finishes as soon as the source ended; `_inflaterStarved`, set when the inflater asked for more input and got none (631-635, 662-666), is consulted only for the zlib/gzip messages (514, 529). DeflateStream itself returns 0 on truncated input without throwing (checked on .NET 8: half of a raw stream decodes to 48,544 of 100,000 bytes with no exception). The class comment promises that a truncated body fails with InvalidDataException (lines 21-23). Tests cover truncated gzip and zlib only (DecompressionBodilessAndTruncationTests, DecompressionZlibAndMultiMemberTests.ZlibDeflate_TruncatedInsideAdler32_Fails).

**Failure scenario.** A close-delimited HTTP/1.x response (no Content-Length, no chunking) with raw deflate is cut by a connection drop, or a buggy origin truncates the coded stream inside otherwise valid framing: the caller receives a partial body as a successful response.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 section 8.4.1.2; RFC 1951

## Suggested fix
Treat an inflater that starved before reporting its final block as truncation for raw DEFLATE as well (validate the `_inflaterStarved` signal on Unity's Mono/IL2CPP DeflateStream first, where zlib may ask for input once more before returning Z_STREAM_END), and add a truncated raw-deflate test for both paths.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A raw-DEFLATE body whose input ends before the final block raises UHttpException with a truncation message
- [ ] Complete raw-DEFLATE bodies decode unchanged
- [ ] The starved-inflater signal is validated on Unity Mono/IL2CPP DeflateStream before relying on it
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ feeding a truncated raw-DEFLATE stream; it fails before the fix

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-protocol-11` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: For Format.RawDeflate EndBody goes to Phase.RawDrain (InflateLayerStream.cs:461-466) and TryDrainRaw finishes as soon as the source ended (:543-555) without consulting _inflaterStarved, which only the gzip and zlib trailer paths use (:514, :529). Measured with a copy of InflateLayerStream.cs on .NET 8: a raw DEFLATE stream cut in half ends as a clean EOF after 49,939 of 100,000 bytes, contrary to the class comment (:21-23). Tests cover truncated gzip and zlib only (DecompressionZlibAndMultiMemberTests.cs:34, :50). Lowered to low: raw DEFLATE under 'deflate' is itself a server error, and the transport's framing (Content-Length, chunked, HTTP/2 END_STREAM) already fails a connection-level truncation, so this needs a close-delimited HTTP/1.x body or an origin that truncates inside valid framing.

Related: [[R11-mw-protocol-29]], [[R11-mw-runtime-03]].

title: [Middleware] On Mono/IL2CPP the inflater's Read blocks until the destination is full, so streamed compressed bodies arrive in destination-sized quanta
body:
## Summary
DecompressionBodySource passes the caller's whole destination to InflateLayerStream, which forwards it to DeflateStream. On Unity's DeflateStream the native read keeps pulling input until the destination is full or the stream ends. A slow streamed gzip body (for example server-sent events or progress downloads) is delivered late and in large chunks instead of as data arrives.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/InflateLayerStream.cs:628`

## Problem
DecompressionBodySource.ReadAsync passes the caller's whole destination to the decoder (DecompressionHandler.cs:313-317) and InflateLayerStream forwards it to DeflateStream (InflateLayerStream.cs:178, 228). Unity's DeflateStream.Read calls the native ReadZStream once per read (System.dll IL: ReadInternal -> DeflateStreamNative.ReadZStream); Mono's zlib helper loops `while (avail_out > 0)` and calls the managed feeder (UnmanagedRead -> our ReadForInflater -> blocking `_source.Read`, InflateLayerStream.cs:618-628) each time its input is used up, returning early only at stream end or when the feeder returns 0. ReadForInflater never returns 0 before the source ends, so a read returns only when `destination.Length` decoded bytes exist. The native loop is recalled from Mono's zlib-helper.c, not read from Unity's binary here; .NET's managed DeflateStream returns as soon as it has output, so the Editor-less dotnet test run cannot show it.

**Failure scenario.** A gzip-encoded event stream (server flushes a 200-byte message every second with Z_SYNC_FLUSH) is consumed with SendStreamingAsync and a 16 KB buffer on an Android IL2CPP player: the first ReadAsync returns only after about 16 KB of decoded messages have accumulated (over a minute), or at end of stream. Combined with mw-runtime-02 the read cannot be cancelled while it waits. To confirm: PlayMode test on Mono with a source that yields one sync-flushed gzip block and then holds; assert ReadAsync returns the block.

## Suggested fix
Same change as mw-runtime-03: never block in the feeder; return 0 from it when no input is buffered so the native loop returns the bytes produced so far, and refill asynchronously.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A streamed compressed body is delivered to the consumer as soon as decoded bytes are available, without waiting for the destination to fill
- [ ] The feeder returns 0 when no input is buffered and the layer refills asynchronously
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ with a trickling compressed source asserting early partial reads; it fails before the fix
- [ ] Verified on Unity Mono and IL2CPP player builds and recorded

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-runtime-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: platform-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Confirmed against Unity's own sources, not only recalled Mono code: Editor/Data/il2cpp/libil2cpp/mono/MonoPosixHelper.cpp:170-220 (2021.3.45f2) ReadZStream loops `while (zs->avail_out > 0)`, calls the managed feeder whenever avail_in == 0, and leaves the loop only on Z_STREAM_END or on Z_BUF_ERROR with no new input (feeder returned 0). The feeder is DeflateStreamNative.UnmanagedRead -> Stream.Read -> InflaterInput.Read -> ReadForInflater (InflateLayerStream.cs:618-639), which returns 0 only after the source ended (625-635); otherwise it blocks in `_source.Read`. DecompressionBodySource passes the caller's whole destination down (DecompressionHandler.cs:313-317, InflateLayerStream.cs:228). So on IL2CPP (and Mono, same helper lineage) a streamed read returns only when the destination is full or the member ends; a sync-flushed partial block is held back. No test covers incremental delivery (no flush/held-source test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware). Edge case (compressed incremental streams such as SSE behind a compressing proxy), hence medium; not run on a device.

Related: [[R11-mw-runtime-03]].

title: [Middleware] gzip CRC32 and zlib Adler-32 are computed one byte per step over all decoded output
body:
## Summary
UpdateCrc32 does one table lookup per byte and UpdateAdler32 is a per-byte loop, both run on the reading thread for every decoded chunk. For large compressed downloads this makes checksum work a measurable share of CPU time.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/InflateLayerStream.cs:712`

## Problem
UpdateCrc32 (InflateLayerStream.cs:712-719) does one 256-entry table lookup per byte and Observe calls it for every decoded chunk (671-682); UpdateAdler32 (684-705) is a per-byte loop as well. The checksum runs on the same thread right after the inflater produced the bytes, for every gzip response.

**Failure scenario.** Decoding a 32 MB gzip body (the default limit) on a mid-range ARM phone spends on the order of 100 ms in the bytewise CRC in addition to inflate; for typical API bodies the cost is small but proportional on every response.

## Suggested fix
Use a slicing-by-4 or slicing-by-8 table (static uint[8][256], no unsafe code needed) for CRC32; unroll the Adler loop over the 5552-byte blocks.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CRC32 uses a slicing-by-4 or slicing-by-8 table without unsafe code
- [ ] Adler-32 processes input in blocks of up to 5552 bytes with deferred modulo
- [ ] Checksum throughput improves by a measured factor recorded in the PR, and results equal the reference for all test vectors
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ comparing against a bytewise reference over random inputs and chunk splits

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-runtime-20` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: performance.

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.

title: [Middleware] Redirect-hop observer, interceptor roles and the auth-skip key are internal, so third parties cannot build the same features
body:
## Summary
IRedirectResponseObserver is internal and is the only way an interceptor outside the redirect interceptor sees consumed 3xx responses and hop requests. Interceptor roles and the auth-skip request key are internal too. Third-party interceptors cannot replicate first-party redirect, auth and ordering behaviour. #76 covers the request derivation and discard primitives but not these contracts.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectHandler.cs:17`

## Problem
Beyond the primitives #76 lists (CopyWithSharedContent, CreateDerived, ResponseBodyDiscardHelper), this slice uses: IRedirectResponseObserver, internal, the only way an interceptor outside the redirect interceptor sees consumed 3xx responses and hop requests (RedirectHandler.cs:17-29, 87-109; only CookieInterceptor implements it, and AuthInterceptor in another assembly cannot, see mw-design-12); IInterceptorRole/InterceptorRole, internal (InterceptorOrdering.cs:10-26), so a replacement redirect or auth interceptor cannot take part in ordering checks and still triggers the 'FollowRedirects without RedirectInterceptor' warning (UHttpClient.cs:146-161); AuthInterceptor.SkipAuthMetadataKey, internal (AuthInterceptor.cs:32), so a custom IAuthTokenProvider that calls its token endpoint through the same client re-enters GetTokenAsync with no supported opt-out; UHttpRequest.SetTimeoutInternal (RedirectInterceptor.cs:172), HandlerCallbackException (RedirectHandler.cs:311), SegmentedBuffer and DetachedBufferedBody construction (SegmentedResponseBodySource.cs:77). Cookie and redirect are additionally coupled through string state keys on the public RequestContext (RedirectHandler.cs:33-34, CookieInterceptor.cs:37-38).

**Failure scenario.** A studio writes its own HSTS, signed-request or per-hop auth interceptor and places it outside RedirectInterceptor: it never sees the intermediate responses or hop requests. A custom refresh provider that reuses the authenticated client recurses until the stack or the refresh gate fails.

## Suggested fix
When #76 promotes the derivation and discard primitives, include a public redirect-hop observer registration, a public role/ordering declaration and a public 'skip auth' request option, and replace the string state keys with typed accessors.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A public redirect-hop observer registration exists with XML docs
- [ ] A public role or ordering declaration for interceptors exists, replacing the internal mechanism
- [ ] A public request option to skip auth replaces the internal key
- [ ] Test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ implements each contract from a test assembly without InternalsVisibleTo

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-design-19` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Mostly as described and under the umbrella of open #76 (no public primitives for third-party interceptors), whose acceptance criteria list only request derivation and body discard. Verified internal: IRedirectResponseObserver and AddResponseObserver (Runtime/Middleware/RedirectHandler.cs:17, 87), IInterceptorRole/InterceptorRole (Runtime/Core/Pipeline/InterceptorOrdering.cs:10, 23) so a third-party redirect interceptor still triggers the once-only FollowRedirects warning (UHttpClient.cs:146-161), AuthInterceptor.SkipAuthMetadataKey (AuthInterceptor.cs:32), UHttpRequest.SetTimeoutInternal (UHttpRequest.cs:496), HandlerCallbackException (Core/HandlerCallbackException.cs:5), SegmentedBuffer (Core/Internal/SegmentedBuffer.cs:29). Corrections: DetachedBufferedBody is a public struct with public constructors (Runtime/Core/DetachedBufferedBody.cs:16-31), so that item is wrong; the 'custom provider recurses' scenario is overstated because a provider can use a separate UHttpClient or pass the literal key "turbohttp.auth.skip" to the public WithMetadata (UHttpRequest.cs:341), unsupported but working; and an interceptor that needs every hop can be placed inside RedirectInterceptor, where it sees each hop itself (RedirectHandler.cs:75-77 comment). What remains is an extension of #76's scope (redirect-hop observer, role declaration, skip-auth option), worth adding to that issue, not a separate defect.

Related: #76, [[R11-mw-runtime-11]].

title: [Middleware] RedirectInterceptor allocates redirect bookkeeping (HashSet, List, TaskCompletionSource) eagerly for every request
body:
## Summary
With FollowRedirects on, each request creates a RedirectHandler with a HashSet<string>, a List<string>, a TaskCompletionSource, adds the initial URI string, and boxes scope-depth ints. Most requests are never redirected, so this is wasted allocation on the common path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectHandler.cs:43`

## Problem
Per request with FollowRedirects on: RedirectHandler with a HashSet<string>, a List<string> and a TaskCompletionSource (RedirectHandler.cs:43-46), `_redirectChain.Add(initialRequest.Uri.AbsoluteUri)` (73), three metadata lookups in ResolveOptions (RedirectInterceptor.cs:76-82), and Enter/ExitRedirectScope, which box an int twice and take the RequestContext lock four times (RedirectHandler.cs:112-122; RequestContext.cs:136-158), plus the async state machine of Wrap.

**Failure scenario.** Every non-redirected request pays about ten small allocations (roughly 500-700 B) and four context-lock round trips for loop detection and chain tracking it never uses.

## Suggested fix
Create `_visitedTargets` and `_redirectChain` on the first redirect, keep the scope depth in a field of a context-attached object (or a pre-boxed value) instead of re-boxing ints.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The visited-target set and redirect chain are created on the first redirect
- [ ] Scope depth is held without re-boxing ints per request
- [ ] A non-redirected request allocates measurably less than before; the count is recorded in the PR
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ asserting allocation bound for a non-redirected request, and unchanged behaviour for redirect chains

## Context

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.

title: [Middleware] Redirect URLs reach exception messages and timeline events unredacted (query values, user-info), bypassing RedactionPolicy
body:
## Summary
RedirectHandler and RedirectInterceptor embed full URLs in exception messages ('Blocked insecure redirect downgrade', 'Redirect loop detected', 'Invalid redirect Location header') and record hops in context state and timeline events. Query values and user-info can contain tokens or passwords, and they leak into logs, monitors and recordings regardless of the redaction setting.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectHandler.cs:186`

## Problem
Messages embed full URLs: RedirectHandler.cs:186 (`Blocked insecure redirect downgrade from '{_currentRequest.Uri}' to '{targetUri}'`), 198 (`Redirect loop detected for target '{targetUri}'`), RedirectInterceptor.cs:114 (`Invalid redirect Location header '{location}'`). RedirectHandler.cs:229-236 stores the `RedirectChain` state and a `Redirect` event with `from`/`to` AbsoluteUri. LoggingHandler.LogError prints error.Message verbatim (Observability/LoggingHandler.cs:229) and MonitorInterceptor copies timeline data with value.ToString() (MonitorInterceptor.cs:661-690) and the error text (705) without the RedactionPolicy that redacts query values and user-info of the captured request URL by default (RedactionPolicy.cs:10-11, MonitorInterceptor.cs:376). The transport keeps even the host out of its messages (RawSocketTransport.cs:484).

**Failure scenario.** An API answers 302 to a pre-signed URL (`...?X-Amz-Signature=...`), an OAuth callback (`?code=...`) or a Location with `user:pass@`. The monitor timeline shows the full `to` URL although the capture URL is redacted, and a blocked downgrade, loop or invalid Location puts the signed URL into the exception message that LoggingInterceptor and crash reporters print.

## Suggested fix
Keep URLs out of redirect exception messages (or reduce them to scheme and host) and record hops in a form observability can redact: strip query and user-info before RecordEvent/SetState, or store Uri objects and apply RedactUrl in the monitor.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Redirect exception messages contain no query string or user-info (scheme and host at most)
- [ ] Timeline events and context state record hops with query and user-info stripped or redactable by the policy
- [ ] The default configuration never emits a redirect URL secret into messages, events or state
- [ ] Regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ with a Location containing user:pass@ and ?token=; it fails before the fix

title: [Middleware] RedirectHandler writes a RedirectChain context state on every hop that nothing reads

title: [Middleware] RedirectHandler dispatches the next hop inside the previous hop's response callback, so same-host redirects deadlock with ConcurrencyInterceptor
body:
## Summary
RedirectHandler awaits the dispatch of the next hop from inside OnResponseStartAsync of the previous hop. The previous hop's inner interceptors, including ConcurrencyInterceptor, are therefore still inside their next call and still hold their permits when the next hop asks for one. With the sample configuration (maxConnectionsPerHost: 2) or the default limit of 6, redirected requests wait on each other and never complete unless the caller cancels. Every user combining RedirectInterceptor and ConcurrencyInterceptor is affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectHandler.cs:242`

## Problem
RedirectHandler.OnResponseStartAsync (RedirectHandler.cs:132-266) awaits `_dispatch(newRequest, this, _context, _cancellationToken)` at :242, i.e. while the previous hop's transport is still awaiting the handler callback (RawSocketTransport.cs:1889 in EmitParsedResponseHeadAsync; Http2Stream.cs:651-665), so the previous hop's `next(...)` has not returned for any interceptor below Redirect. ConcurrencyInterceptor.cs:60-70 acquires before `next` and releases in `finally` after it returns, so hop N still holds its permit when hop N+1 calls ConcurrencyLimiter.AcquireAsync (ConcurrencyLimiter.cs:92-101: one global and one per-authority semaphore, cancellable only by the caller token or dispose). The request deadline exists only inside the transport (RawSocketTransport.cs:439-440 CancelAfter), which hop N+1 never reaches; ApplyTotalRedirectTimeoutBudget (RedirectInterceptor.cs:155-174) only shortens request.Timeout. The documented canonical order puts Redirect (#2) outside Concurrency (#8) (Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:55-62, 'Holds a permit only while a request is on the wire'), and Samples~/05-AdvancedFeatures/AdvancedFeaturesExample.cs:44,63 ships RedirectInterceptor + ConcurrencyInterceptor(maxConnectionsPerHost: 2). No test combines the two interceptors (rg over Tests/Runtime: only InterceptorOrderTests names both).

**Failure scenario.** Sample 05 client, GET https://httpbin.org/redirect/2 (three hops on one authority): hops 1 and 2 hold both per-host permits, hop 3 waits for a third and the request never completes unless the caller cancels its own token. With the default limit of 6: six concurrent requests that each get one same-host 302 each hold one permit and wait for a second, so all six hang and every later request to that host queues behind them. Every hop also takes a global permit, so long cross-host chains shrink maxTotalConnections the same way.

## Suggested fix
Unwind before re-dispatching: let RedirectHandler discard the 3xx body, record the next hop request and return, and have RedirectInterceptor.Wrap loop `await next(hopRequest, redirectHandler, ...)` after the previous `next` returned, so each hop releases what its inner interceptors hold. Add a test with ConcurrencyInterceptor(1, 1) and a same-host redirect.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each redirect hop releases the permits and other resources held by its inner interceptors before the next hop is dispatched.
- [ ] GET through RedirectInterceptor and ConcurrencyInterceptor(1, 1) with a same-host redirect chain completes without caller cancellation.
- [ ] Six concurrent requests that each receive one same-host 302 under the default concurrency limit all complete.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it (combines the two interceptors).

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-runtime-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: RedirectHandler.OnResponseStartAsync awaits _dispatch(newRequest, this, ...) for the next hop (RedirectHandler.cs:242) while the previous hop's transport is still awaiting that callback (RawSocketTransport.cs:1889-1894; HTTP/2: Http2Stream.cs:651-667, the dispatch awaits the completion set after the handler returns). The handlers between forward the callback inline (Retry/RetryDetectorHandler.cs:81/94, Cache/CacheStoringHandler.cs:62-160), so the previous hop's ConcurrencyInterceptor is still inside 'await next' and holds its permit until the finally (RateLimit/ConcurrencyInterceptor.cs:60-70). The next hop's AcquireAsync waits on the caller token and the limiter's dispose token only (ConcurrencyLimiter.cs:92-101); the request deadline lives in the transport of each hop (RawSocketTransport.cs:439-440), which the waiting hop never reaches, and ApplyTotalRedirectTimeoutBudget only shortens request.Timeout (RedirectInterceptor.cs:155-174). No ordering rule covers Redirect/Concurrency (InterceptorOrdering.cs:53-70); the documented canonical order puts Redirect (#2) outside Concurrency (#8) (Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:55-62) and Samples~/05-AdvancedFeatures/AdvancedFeaturesExample.cs:44,63 ships exactly that with maxConnectionsPerHost: 2, so a same-authority chain of three hops never completes. No test combines the two interceptors.

title: [Docs] Public Middleware API lacks XML documentation and several result types are mutable
body:
## Summary
Many public members of the Middleware modules (RedirectInterceptor, CookieJar, CookieInterceptor, DefaultHeadersInterceptor, OAuthClient, OAuthToken, PkceUtility, token stores) have no XML documentation, including behaviour-defining constructor parameters. OAuthAuthorizationRequest and OpenIdProviderMetadata are library outputs with public setters, and StaticTokenProvider is unsealed without virtual members. The project rules require XML docs on public API, and the API baseline freezes at GA.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:23`

## Problem
Undocumented public members: RedirectInterceptor constructor (four behaviour switches) and Wrap (RedirectInterceptor.cs:23-38); CookieSameSite (CookieJar.cs:10-16); CookieJar.Count, GetDomainCount, StoreFromSetCookieHeaders, GetCookieHeader, Dispose (CookieJar.cs:170-360); CookieInterceptor.Jar, constructor, Wrap, Dispose; DefaultHeadersInterceptor constructor; OAuthClient.ResolveEndpointsAsync, DiscoverAsync, GetValidTokenAsync, BuildTokenStoreKey, IsTokenExpired, ValidateState, Dispose (OAuthClient.cs:92, 224, 251, 276, 283, 291, 302); all of OAuthToken, PkceUtility, OAuthTokenProvider and InMemoryTokenStore; the properties of OAuthAuthorizationRequest, OAuthCodeExchangeRequest, OAuthRefreshRequest and OpenIdProviderMetadata (OAuthConfig.cs:87-120). OAuthAuthorizationRequest and OpenIdProviderMetadata are outputs of the library yet have public setters; StaticTokenProvider is an unsealed class with no virtual member. CLAUDE.md section 4 requires XML docs on public API.

**Failure scenario.** A user cannot learn from IntelliSense that GetValidTokenAsync may return an expired token or null, that StoreFromSetCookieHeaders silently ignores rejected cookies, or what defaultEnforceRedirectTotalTimeout changes; the mutable result types let calling code alter State or CodeVerifier between the two legs of the flow by accident.

## Suggested fix
Document the listed members (thread-safety, null/expired return values, ownership), make the result types read-only, and seal StaticTokenProvider before the API baseline freezes at GA.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every public member listed in the finding has an XML doc comment stating thread-safety, null/expired return values and ownership where relevant.
- [ ] OAuthAuthorizationRequest and OpenIdProviderMetadata expose read-only properties, and StaticTokenProvider is sealed.
- [ ] The shadow build with analyzers (Tools~/ci/check.sh) passes with no new warning.

title: [Middleware] RedirectInterceptor hangs when the first inner dispatch returns without a terminal callback
body:
## Summary
RedirectInterceptor.Wrap awaits redirectHandler.Completion after the first next call without checking that a terminal callback was delivered. Nested hops have such a guard, but the first dispatch does not, and the await is not linked to the cancellation token. If an inner interceptor or stub returns without calling OnResponseStartAsync or OnResponseError, the request never completes and cancelling does not release it.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:66`

## Problem
Wrap does `await next(request, redirectHandler, ...)` and then `await redirectHandler.Completion` (RedirectInterceptor.cs:66-67). Completion is only resolved from the handler callbacks (RedirectHandler.cs:148-152, 293-304). The nested hop dispatch has the guard `if (!_completion.Task.IsCompleted) TrySetException("Redirect pipeline completed without delivering a terminal callback.")` (RedirectHandler.cs:242-247, covered by RedirectInterceptorTests.cs:968), and Core's bridges have the same check (ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:126-138, StreamingDispatchBridge.cs:229), but that check can never run here because the outer dispatch task is itself blocked on Completion. The await is not linked to the cancellation token either.

**Failure scenario.** An interceptor or test transport inside the redirect interceptor returns a completed task without calling OnResponseStartAsync or OnResponseError (a short-circuiting stub, or a bug). Without RedirectInterceptor the caller gets "Pipeline completed without delivering a response"; with it SendBufferedAsync never completes, no timeout fires (no transport is running) and cancelling the token does not release it.

## Suggested fix
After the first `await next(...)`, apply the same check as the nested path: if Completion is not completed, fail it with the terminal-callback error before awaiting it. Add the mirror of the existing nested-hop test for the first dispatch.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After the first await next(...), a Completion that is not completed is failed with the terminal-callback error (UHttpException) instead of being awaited indefinitely.
- [ ] The behaviour matches the nested-hop guard and Core's 'Pipeline completed without delivering a response' error.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it and mirrors the existing nested-hop test for the first dispatch.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-design-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: Wrap awaits `next(...)` and then `redirectHandler.Completion` with no check and no token link (RedirectInterceptor.cs:66-67); Completion is resolved only from handler callbacks (RedirectHandler.cs:148-152, 293-304). The nested hop has the guard (RedirectHandler.cs:242-247, tested at RedirectInterceptorTests.cs:968) and Core's collector has it too (ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:126-138), so the first dispatch is the one unguarded place. It needs an inner dispatch that breaks the pipeline contract (returns normally without a terminal callback); I found no first-party path that does, which is why this is low: a missing defensive check that turns a diagnosable error into a hang.

Also reported as `mw-runtime-09` (merged into this issue).

title: [Middleware] Credential-bearing header set is defined four times and the redirect scrub cannot be extended beyond Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie
body:
## Summary
RedirectInterceptor hard-codes three headers to strip on cross-origin redirects, while RedactionPolicy lists 13 sensitive names and RecordReplayTransport keeps two more lists. The same-origin comparison is also written three times (redirect, auth, cache). A custom header such as X-Api-Key is treated as secret by the monitor but forwarded on a cross-origin redirect, and the app has no supported way to add it to the scrub.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:133`

## Problem
RedirectInterceptor.BuildRedirectRequest hard-codes three names (RedirectInterceptor.cs:133-138) and has no parameter for more. Observability's RedactionPolicy.DefaultHeaderNames lists 13 names including X-Api-Key, Api-Key, X-Auth-Token, X-Amz-Security-Token, X-Goog-Api-Key, X-CSRF-Token, X-XSRF-Token (RedactionPolicy.cs:23-38); Testing's RecordReplayTransport keeps two more copies (RecordReplayTransport.cs:130-145 and 238-242); the transport strips Proxy-Authorization separately (RawSocketTransport.cs:1342,1360). The origin comparison is also written three times: RedirectInterceptor.IsCrossOrigin (176-181), AuthInterceptor.IsBoundOrigin (AuthInterceptor.cs:125-127) and CacheInterceptor.IsSameAuthority (CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:281-288). Core has no shared definition, so each module decides alone what a credential is.

**Failure scenario.** A game backend key set as options.DefaultHeaders["X-Api-Key"] is treated as a secret by the monitor and by recordings, but a 302 to another origin forwards it unchanged, and the app has no supported way to add it to the redirect scrub.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 section 15.4

## Suggested fix
Put one sensitive-request-header set and one same-origin comparison in Core (public, so third-party interceptors can use them) and consume them from redirect, auth, cache, redaction and record/replay. Give RedirectInterceptor an option to extend the cross-origin scrub list.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Core exposes one sensitive-request-header set and one same-origin comparison, consumed by redirect, auth, cache, redaction and record/replay.
- [ ] RedirectInterceptor offers an option to extend the cross-origin scrub list; a 302 to another origin removes a header added through it.
- [ ] The default scrub still removes Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie as RFC 9110 section 15.4 expects.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-design-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Facts hold: the redirect scrub hard-codes three names with no extension point (RedirectInterceptor.cs:133-138); RedactionPolicy.DefaultHeaderNames has 13 (RedactionPolicy.cs:23-38); RecordReplayTransport keeps two more lists (RecordReplayTransport.cs:130-145, 238-242); the origin comparison exists in RedirectInterceptor.IsCrossOrigin (176-181), AuthInterceptor.IsBoundOrigin (125-127) and CacheInterceptor.IsSameAuthority (CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:280). Severity lowered: stripping Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie is what RFC 9110 section 15.4 names and what other clients do, so forwarding a custom X-Api-Key header is not a protocol defect; this is duplication plus a missing option. Open issue #117 (acceptance: 'no module keeps its own list') covers unifying the redaction lists but not the redirect scrub list or a shared same-origin helper, so known_issue is left 0.

Related: #117.

title: [Middleware] IsCrossSiteRequest metadata is filled with a per-hop cross-origin flag, so SameSite cookies are evaluated per hop on origins
body:
## Summary
BuildRedirectRequest sets IsCrossSiteRequest to whether the previous hop and target differ in scheme, host or port. CookieJar uses it to withhold SameSite cookies, so a same-site redirect between hosts withholds Lax cookies a browser would send, and the flag resets on the hop after a cross-origin one. The key name does not describe what it carries.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:141`

## Problem
BuildRedirectRequest sets metadata[RequestMetadataKeys.IsCrossSiteRequest] = crossOrigin, where crossOrigin compares scheme, host and port of the previous hop and the target (RedirectInterceptor.cs:141, 176-181; RedirectHandler.cs:203). CookieJar.SameSiteAllows uses the flag to withhold SameSite=Strict cookies and SameSite=Lax cookies on non-safe methods (CookieJar.cs:695-707; CookieInterceptor.cs:113-119). The comment in AuthRedirectOrderTests.cs:54-55 notes that the flag is false again on the hop after a cross-origin one.

**Failure scenario.** POST https://api.example.com/login answers 307 to https://auth.example.com/login (same site, different host): the jar withholds auth.example.com's SameSite=Lax session cookie, which a browser would send for a same-site request. A->B->B: the third hop is flagged same-site although the chain started on A, so B's Strict cookies are sent on it but not on the second hop.

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 section 5.4

## Suggested fix
Either rename the key to what it carries and document that SameSite is evaluated per hop on origins, or compute a site comparison (registrable domain through the jar's public-suffix predicate) against the first request of the chain.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Either IsCrossSiteRequest is computed as a site comparison (registrable domain via the jar's public-suffix predicate) against the first request of the chain, or the key is renamed and documented as a per-hop origin flag.
- [ ] POST api.example.com -> 307 auth.example.com sends auth.example.com's SameSite=Lax cookie (same site) under the chosen semantics.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it covering a multi-hop chain with SameSite cookies.

## Context

title: [Middleware] RedirectInterceptor overwrites IsCrossSiteRequest per hop, so a cross-site chain becomes same-site on its next same-origin hop
body:
## Summary
Each redirect hop sets IsCrossSiteRequest to the cross-origin result of the previous and next hop only, replacing a caller-supplied true with false on a same-origin redirect. After A -> B -> B', the last hop is treated as same-site and CookieJar attaches B's SameSite=Strict and Lax cookies although the chain started on another site.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:141`

## Problem
BuildRedirectRequest sets `metadata[RequestMetadataKeys.IsCrossSiteRequest] = crossOrigin` (141), where crossOrigin compares only the previous and the next hop (RedirectHandler.cs:203). A caller-supplied `true` is replaced by `false` on a same-origin redirect, and after A -> B (true) the hop B -> B' gets `false`. CookieJar.SameSiteAllows (695-707) relies on this flag alone. No test covers a multi-hop chain with SameSite cookies.

**Failure scenario.** A request the application marked cross-site (or a chain that left site A for site B) is redirected by B to another URL on B: the SameSite=Strict and Lax cookies of B are attached to that hop although the chain started on another site.

## Spec reference
RFC 6265bis section 5.2 (same-site requests and redirect chains)

## Suggested fix
Make the flag sticky: `existing || crossOrigin`, evaluated against the first request of the chain.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The flag stays true once a chain has crossed sites (existing || crossOrigin), evaluated against the first request of the chain.
- [ ] A caller-supplied true is not reset by a same-origin redirect.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it with an A -> B -> B' chain and SameSite cookies.

title: [Middleware] Redirect loop detection keys on the target URL only, so 307 followed by 303 to the same URL is reported as a loop
body:
## Summary
RedirectHandler records each target URL in a visited set and fails on a repeat regardless of the method used for the follow-up. POST /old -> 307 /form -> 303 /form (post/redirect/get) repeats the key and fails with 'Redirect loop detected' although the follow-up is a different request.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:189`

## Problem
BuildLoopKey (189-201) is scheme://host[:port]/path?query; RedirectHandler adds each target to _visitedTargets and fails on a repeat (RedirectHandler.cs:191-201) regardless of the method the follow-up uses. The first request URL is not in the set, which hides the problem for a direct POST -> 303 to the same URL.

**Failure scenario.** `POST /old` -> `307 Location: /form` (POST /form, key added) -> `303 Location: /form` (post/redirect/get on the new URL): the GET /form target repeats the key and the request fails with 'Redirect loop detected' although no loop exists.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 section 15.4.4

## Suggested fix
Include the follow-up method in the loop key (or rely on the redirect limit alone, as browsers do).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The loop key includes the follow-up method (or loop detection relies on the redirect limit alone) per RFC 9110 section 15.4.4.
- [ ] POST -> 307 /form -> 303 /form completes with the final response; a true same-method loop still fails with a redirect error.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it.

title: [Middleware] Redirect that drops the request body keeps Expect, Content-Encoding, Content-Language and Content-Location on the GET
body:
## Summary
RemoveBodyHeaders removes only Content-Length, Content-Type and Transfer-Encoding. When a 303 turns a POST into a bodiless GET, Expect: 100-continue and the other content-specific fields remain. RFC 9110 section 10.1.1 forbids a 100-continue expectation without content, and servers may answer 417.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:203`

## Problem
RemoveBodyHeaders removes only Content-Length, Content-Type and Transfer-Encoding (203-208). `Expect: 100-continue` set through UHttpRequest (Core/UHttpRequest.cs:311-322) stays in the cloned headers (126), and the transport only waits for 100 when there is a body but still serializes the header. RFC 9110 section 10.1.1: a client MUST NOT generate a 100-continue expectation in a request without content; section 15.4 lists the content-specific fields to remove when the method changes to GET.

**Failure scenario.** POST with `Expect: 100-continue` and `Content-Encoding: gzip` gets a 303: the follow-up is `GET` with `Expect: 100-continue` and `Content-Encoding: gzip` and no body; servers that reject unexpected Expect answer 417, which is returned to the caller because the transport's 417 repeat only applies to requests with a body.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 sections 10.1.1, 15.4

## Suggested fix
When DropsBody is set also remove Expect, Content-Encoding, Content-Language, Content-Location and Digest/Content-MD5.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When the redirect drops the body, Expect, Content-Encoding, Content-Language, Content-Location and Digest/Content-MD5 are removed along with the existing headers.
- [ ] A POST with Expect: 100-continue and Content-Encoding: gzip answered by 303 produces a GET carrying none of them.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it.

## Context

title: [Middleware] Body-preserving redirect copies the whole buffered request body per hop and clones headers and metadata twice
body:
## Summary
CreateRedirectContent clones every replayable non-stream body with CloneDetached, which copies the byte array, although the source request outlives the chain. BuildRedirectRequest clones headers and metadata and CreateDerived clones them again, and superseded hop requests are never disposed. A 20 MB buffered POST redirected twice allocates two extra 20 MB arrays on the large object heap, which matters on mobile.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:239`

## Problem
CreateRedirectContent returns `RedirectContent.Owned(content.CloneDetached())` for every replayable non-stream body (RedirectInterceptor.cs:239); BufferedRequestBody/OwnedMemoryRequestBody.CloneDetachedCore copy with `ToArray()` (UHttpRequestBody.cs:321-326, 373-379), while stream bodies are shared (234-237). The source request outlives the whole chain (RedirectHandler keeps `_currentRequest`, the caller's request owns the content until the send ends), so a shared-content hop would be safe. BuildRedirectRequest clones headers (126) and metadata (140) and CreateDerived's constructor clones both again (UHttpRequest.cs:144-150). RedirectHandler never disposes `newRequest` (RedirectHandler.cs:207-238); harmless today only because the clones hold no pooled memory.

**Failure scenario.** POST of a 20 MB buffered upload answered by 307 to a storage host and then 308 to a regional host: two extra 20 MB arrays on the large object heap in addition to the original, on a memory-constrained phone.

## Suggested fix
Share the content for all replayable bodies (`ownsContent: false`) instead of CloneDetached, pass the already-cloned headers/metadata through without a second copy, and dispose superseded hop requests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Replayable bodies are shared across hops (ownsContent: false) instead of copied; a 307/308 chain allocates no additional body-sized arrays.
- [ ] Headers and metadata are cloned once per hop, and superseded hop requests are disposed.

title: [Middleware] RedirectInterceptor defaultFollowRedirects and defaultMaxRedirects constructor arguments are ignored for client-created requests
body:
## Summary
UHttpClient.CreateRequest always writes FollowRedirects and MaxRedirects metadata from UHttpClientOptions, and RedirectInterceptor uses its constructor values only when the metadata key is absent. For every request created through the client the constructor arguments are dead, although Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:93 shows new RedirectInterceptor(defaultMaxRedirects: 5) as the way to set the limit.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs:265`

## Problem
ResolveFollowRedirects/ResolveMaxRedirects use the constructor value only when the request metadata has no entry (RedirectInterceptor.cs:265-290). UHttpClient.CreateRequest always calls ApplyDefaultMetadata, which writes RequestMetadataKeys.FollowRedirects and MaxRedirects from UHttpClientOptions on every request (UHttpClient.cs:182-183, 749-750; options default true / 10, UHttpClientOptions.cs:98,104). So for client.Get/Post/... the metadata is always present and the constructor defaults are dead. Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:93 shows `new RedirectInterceptor(defaultMaxRedirects: 5)` as the configuration example. The tests that pass constructor values (RedirectInterceptorTests.cs:74, 566, 595, 763) build `new UHttpRequest(...)` without metadata, so they do not see it.

**Failure scenario.** options.Interceptors.Add(new RedirectInterceptor(defaultMaxRedirects: 5)); client.Get(url) follows up to 10 redirects. new RedirectInterceptor(defaultFollowRedirects: false) with default options still follows every redirect, including cross-origin ones the app meant to inspect itself.

## Suggested fix
Have one source of truth: either drop the two constructor parameters (keep the options/metadata path) or let UHttpClient write the metadata only when the option differs from its default / was set explicitly, and fix the documentation snippet. Add a test that sends a client-created request through a RedirectInterceptor with non-default constructor values.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] There is one source of truth: the constructor parameters are removed, or the client writes the metadata only when the option was set explicitly, so new RedirectInterceptor(defaultMaxRedirects: 5) limits client.Get to 5 redirects.
- [ ] The documentation snippet is corrected to match.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ fails before the fix and passes after it sending a client-created request through a RedirectInterceptor with non-default constructor values.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `mw-design-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/mw.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. UHttpClient.CreateRequest always calls ApplyDefaultMetadata (UHttpClient.cs:182-183), which writes FollowRedirects and MaxRedirects from the options on every request (749-750). ResolveFollowRedirects/ResolveMaxRedirects use the constructor value only when the metadata key is absent (RedirectInterceptor.cs:265-290), so for every request created through the client the two constructor arguments are dead. Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:93 shows `new RedirectInterceptor(defaultMaxRedirects: 5)` as the configuration example, two lines after stating the options are what apply. The constructor values only take effect for hand-built `new UHttpRequest(...)` (public constructor, UHttpRequest.cs:115), which is what the tests at RedirectInterceptorTests.cs:74/566/595/763 use.

title: [Packaging] TurboHTTP.Middleware ships cookies, decompression, redirects and default headers as one assembly
body:
## Summary
The Middleware assembly bundles four independent features, so builds that copy assemblies whole (Mono without stripping, or Minimal stripping) carry all of them even if only redirects are used. The reviewer estimates the module at under 100 KB of IL and recommends against a split for size alone; if a split is done, decompression is the self-contained candidate, while cookies depend on redirect internals.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/TurboHTTP.Middleware.asmdef:2`

## Problem
The assembly references only Core and nothing outside it references its types (only doc strings in UHttpClient.cs:151-160 and UHttpClientOptions.cs:94-102; TurboHttpBootstrap does not touch it), there is no link.xml or [Preserve], so with linker reachability an unused interceptor is removed. Where assemblies are copied whole (Mono backend with stripping disabled, or a Minimal stripping level), a project that only wants redirects (718 lines: RedirectInterceptor + RedirectHandler) also gets decompression (1,876 lines in four files, the only user of System.IO.Compression in the module, with a static CRC table) and cookies (1,200 lines, with two static public-suffix sets of about 110 strings, CookieJar.cs:23-114, and ReaderWriterLockSlim). The whole module is about 4,300 source lines; my estimate is well under 100 KB of IL, so the redirect-only saving is roughly 70% of a small assembly. Cookie depends on redirect internals (CookieInterceptor.cs:22, 78-80; RedirectHandler.cs:87-122), so a split needs that contract made public first. The same shape exists in Auth: a bearer-only project carries OAuthClient/PKCE (about 800 of 1,100 lines) next to AuthInterceptor and StaticTokenProvider.

**Failure scenario.** No functional failure. Cost only: redirect-only or bearer-only projects on unstripped builds carry the unused cookie/decompression or OAuth code.

## Suggested fix
Do not split for size alone. If a split is wanted, isolate decompression (self-contained, the heaviest part, the only System.IO.Compression user) and keep redirect and cookies together until the hop-observer contract is public (mw-design-19).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A decision is recorded in the issue or PR on whether decompression is split into its own assembly, with the measured size saving.
- [ ] If split, asmdef references and Tools~/ci/check_repo.py module rules pass and no public type changes namespace without a documented migration.
- [ ] No behaviour change in redirect, cookie or decompression interceptors; existing Tests/Runtime/Middleware/ tests pass.
